source.text: Καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ γάμος ἐγένετο ἐν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἦν ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐκεῖ·

records.literal_gloss: And on the day the third a wedding took place in Cana of the Galilee, and was the mother of the Jesus there.

en.L: And on the third day a wedding took place in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.
en.B: On the third day a wedding was held at Cana in Galilee, and Jesus's mother was there.
en.R: Two days later there was a wedding in the village of Cana in Galilee. Jesus's mother was there.

es.L: Y al tercer día hubo una boda en Caná de Galilea, y la madre de Jesús estaba allí.
es.B: Al tercer día se celebró una boda en Caná de Galilea, y la madre de Jesús estaba allí.
es.R: Dos días después hubo una boda en el pueblo de Caná, en Galilea. La madre de Jesús estaba allí.

fr.L: Et le troisième jour, un mariage eut lieu à Cana de Galilée, et la mère de Jésus était là.
fr.B: Le troisième jour, on célébra un mariage à Cana, en Galilée, et la mère de Jésus s’y trouvait.
fr.R: Deux jours plus tard, il y a eu un mariage dans le village de Cana, en Galilée. La mère de Jésus était là.

sw.L: Na siku ya tatu kulikuwa na harusi katika Kana ya Galilaya, na mama yake Yesu alikuwako huko.
sw.B: Siku ya tatu kulifanyika harusi huko Kana ya Galilaya, na mama yake Yesu alikuwa huko.
sw.R: Siku mbili baadaye kulikuwa na harusi katika kijiji cha Kana huko Galilaya. Mama yake Yesu alikuwa huko.

ko.L: 그리고 셋째 날에 갈릴리의 가나에서 혼인 잔치가 있었고, 예수의 어머니가 거기에 있었다.
ko.B: 셋째 날에 갈릴리 가나에서 혼인 잔치가 열렸는데, 예수의 어머니가 그곳에 있었다.
ko.R: 이틀 뒤에 갈릴리 지방의 가나 마을에서 결혼 잔치가 있었다. 예수의 어머니도 거기에 와 있었다.

vi.L: Và vào ngày thứ ba, có một tiệc cưới tại Ca-na thuộc Ga-li-lê, và mẹ của Đức Giê-xu có ở đó.
vi.B: Ngày thứ ba, có một đám cưới ở Ca-na, xứ Ga-li-lê, và mẹ của Đức Giê-xu có mặt ở đó.
vi.R: Hai ngày sau, có một đám cưới ở làng Ca-na, vùng Ga-li-lê. Mẹ của Đức Giê-xu cũng ở đó.

decisions.choice: on the third day, counted from the last day named (1:43): two days later
alternatives: the third day of the week
decisions.reason: Days were counted inclusively, so the day of the last event counts as the first. John has been marking days since 1:29, 1:35 and 1:43; this continues the count.

decisions.choice: a plain time note that may also carry an echo
alternatives: a deliberate pointer to the resurrection
decisions.reason: "The third day" is the day of the resurrection (compare 2:19 "in three days"), and on the third day God showed himself at Sinai (Exodus 19:11, 16), while this sign reveals Jesus's glory (2:11). John does not draw either link himself, so every level keeps the phrase and makes no claim. Readable gives the plain sense.
The word covers the whole celebration, a feast that could last several days (Judges 14:12, 17). The groom's family provided the food and wine for the guests.

decisions.choice: the mother of Jesus / Jesus's mother, not "Mary"
decisions.reason: John never gives her name (here and at 19:25-27); every level keeps his description.
The plain sense of the inclusive count (m1). Literal and Balanced keep "third day" so that the possible echo (m2) stays visible.
"Las bodas" is the older word and now sounds literary; "una boda" is the everyday Spanish word for the whole celebration (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); John's historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("dit", "appelle")
decisions.reason: The passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative in French and suits a careful public reading; the passé composé is how French is spoken and how young readers now meet stories, so Readable uses it throughout. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level. Literal keeps the present where John tells a past event in the present (2:3, 2:9), as English Literal does; with "dire" the present and the passé simple look the same ("il dit"). This holds for the whole chapter.
"Des noces" is the older word and now sounds literary or archaic; "un mariage" is the everyday French word for the celebration (m3).
The Greek word is the whole wedding celebration, which lasted days, not the ceremony that "결혼식" names. "혼인" is the formal word; Readable uses the everyday "결혼".

source.text: ἐκλήθη δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν γάμον.

records.literal_gloss: Was invited and also the Jesus and the disciples of him to the wedding.

en.L: And Jesus also was invited, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, to the wedding.
en.B: Jesus had been invited to the wedding too, along with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples had been invited to the wedding too.

es.L: Y fue invitado también Jesús, y sus discípulos, a la boda.
es.B: Jesús también había sido invitado a la boda, junto con sus discípulos.
es.R: Jesús y sus discípulos también estaban invitados a la boda.

fr.L: Et Jésus aussi fut invité, ainsi que {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, au mariage.
fr.B: Jésus aussi avait été invité au mariage, avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.
fr.R: Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples avaient été invités au mariage, eux aussi.

sw.L: Na Yesu pia alikuwa amealikwa, na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, kwenye harusi.
sw.B: Yesu pia alikuwa amealikwa kwenye harusi hiyo, pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wamealikwa kwenye harusi pia.

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서도 그분의 제자들과 함께 그 혼인 잔치에 초대를 받으셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서도 제자들과 함께 그 잔치에 초대를 받으셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서도 제자들과 함께 그 결혼 잔치에 초대를 받으셨다.

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu cũng được mời, cùng các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, đến tiệc cưới.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu cũng được mời dự đám cưới, cùng với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng được mời đến dự đám cưới.

decisions.choice: Jesus is the main guest; the disciples come with him
alternatives: Jesus and the disciples invited as equals
decisions.reason: The verb is singular and agrees with Jesus, who is named first; the disciples are added after him.

decisions.choice: the disciples who had begun to follow him in 1:35-51
decisions.reason: John has not yet mentioned the Twelve (first at 6:67). The disciples here are those of chapter 1, among them Andrew, Simon Peter, Philip and Nathanael, who came from Cana (21:2).

decisions.choice: Narrative in the plain written style with the subject honorific for Jesus ("예수께서", "-시-"), and "그분" for "he/him"; no deity_pronoun spans
alternatives: deity_pronoun setting spans, as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Korean. Respect for Jesus is carried at every level by "께서", the honorific "-시-" and "그분", as the Korean style guide sets for the whole book. This holds for the whole of this passage.

source.text: καὶ ὑστερήσαντος οἴνου λέγει ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν· Οἶνον οὐκ ἔχουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And having run short wine, says the mother of the Jesus to him, "Wine not they have."

en.L: And when [the] wine ran short, the mother of Jesus says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "They have no wine."
en.B: When the wine gave out, Jesus's mother said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "They have no wine left."
en.R: When the wine was all gone, Jesus's mother came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "They have run out of wine."

es.L: Y al faltar vino, la madre de Jesús le dice: «No tienen vino».
es.B: Cuando se acabó el vino, la madre de Jesús le dijo: «Ya no tienen vino».
es.R: Cuando ya no quedaba vino, la madre de Jesús fue a decirle: «Se les acabó el vino».

fr.L: Et comme [le] vin venait à manquer, la mère de Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Ils n’ont pas de vin. »
fr.B: Comme le vin manquait, la mère de Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Ils n’ont plus de vin. »
fr.R: Quand tout le vin a été bu, la mère de Jésus est venue {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dire : « Ils n’ont plus de vin. »

sw.L: Na divai ilipopungua, mama yake Yesu anamwambia, "Hawana divai."
sw.B: Divai ilipokwisha, mama yake Yesu alimwambia, "Hawana divai tena."
sw.R: Divai ilipokwisha yote, mama yake Yesu alimjia, akamwambia, "Divai imewaishia."

ko.L: 그리고 포도주가 모자라게 되자, 예수의 어머니가 그분께 말한다. "그들에게 포도주가 없다."
ko.B: 포도주가 다 떨어지자, 예수의 어머니가 예수께 말했다. "저 사람들에게 포도주가 남아 있지 않구나."
ko.R: 포도주가 다 떨어지자, 예수의 어머니가 예수께 와서 말했다. "잔칫집에 포도주가 다 떨어졌구나."

vi.L: Và khi rượu thiếu, mẹ của Đức Giê-xu nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Họ không có rượu."
vi.B: Khi rượu đã cạn, mẹ của Đức Giê-xu nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Họ hết rượu rồi."
vi.R: Khi rượu đã hết sạch, mẹ của Đức Giê-xu đến nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Nhà người ta hết rượu rồi."

decisions.choice: running out of wine would shame the host family
decisions.reason: Hospitality was a serious duty, and the groom's family was expected to provide for the guests through the whole feast (m3 at 2:1). Running out was a public embarrassment.

decisions.choice: a statement of need that hints at a request
alternatives: a direct request for a miracle
decisions.reason: She only states the problem, but she says it to Jesus, and verse 5 shows that she expects him to do something. No level turns it into an explicit request.

alternatives: a longer reading: they had no wine, because the wine of the wedding was used up
decisions.reason: The longer wording is found in the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus and some Old Latin manuscripts. It says the same thing at more length, so the shorter text of the great majority is kept and no footnote is needed. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

John often tells a story in the present tense ("she says") for vividness; here and in the rest of the passage Balanced and Readable use the past, which is normal for a story told in this language. Literal keeps the present.
Readable shows that she brings the problem to him; the words add a movement implied by "to him".
"Divai" is wine made from grapes, the word for the wine of the Lord's Supper in most Swahili churches. "Mvinyo" is also wine but is used of any fermented drink, and "pombe" is beer.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps John's present ("le dice"); Balanced and Readable tell the story in the pretérito, the normal tense of Spanish narrative. This applies throughout the passage.
As in English: Readable shows that she brings the problem to him.

decisions.choice: His mother speaks to him in the plain style a Korean mother uses to a grown son ("-구나")
decisions.reason: The style guide sets the formal polite style for people speaking to Jesus, but that would make his mother sound like a stranger. A mother naturally uses the plain style to her son; she still speaks to him with the honorific dative "께" in the narrative. A reviewer may prefer a softer polite ending.
"Rượu" is any alcoholic drink, but at a wedding feast the context makes it plain that wine is meant, and "rượu nho" (grape wine) repeated through the story would sound stiff.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, γύναι;

records.literal_gloss: And says to her the Jesus, "What to me and to you, woman?"

en.L: And Jesus says to her, "What [is that] to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and to you, Woman?
en.B: Jesus said to her, "Woman, is that a matter for you and {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.R: Jesus answered, "Mother, why are you bringing this to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

es.L: Y Jesús le dice: «¿Qué [nos importa eso] a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y a ti, mujer?
es.B: Jesús le dijo: «Mujer, ¿y eso qué tiene que ver con nosotros?
es.R: Jesús le respondió: «Madre, ¿por qué me lo dices a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}?

fr.L: Et Jésus lui dit : « Qu’[est-ce que cela fait], à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et à toi, Femme ?
fr.B: Jésus lui dit : « Femme, est-ce notre affaire, à toi et à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ?
fr.R: Jésus lui a répondu : « Mère, pourquoi viens-tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dire cela ?

sw.L: Naye Yesu anamwambia, "Ni nini {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} na kwako, Mama?
sw.B: Yesu akamwambia, "Mama, jambo hilo linatuhusu nini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} na wewe?
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Mama, kwa nini unaniletea jambo hili?

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서 그녀에게 말씀하신다. "여자여, 그것이 나와 당신에게 무슨 [상관이 있나요]?
ko.B: 예수께서 어머니에게 말씀하셨다. "어머니, 그것이 어머니와 저의 일인가요?
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "어머니, 왜 그 일을 저에게 말씀하세요?

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu nói với bà: "Thưa bà, [việc đó] có [liên quan] gì đến {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và bà?
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Thưa mẹ, việc ấy liên quan gì đến mẹ và con?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Mẹ ơi, sao mẹ lại nói việc này với con?

decisions.choice: a courteous refusal to be directed: it is not hers to set his course
alternatives: that is no concern of ours (the shortage does not concern us)
decisions.reason: The phrase, literally "what to me and to you", marks distance between two parties. It can be hostile (Judges 11:12; Mark 1:24) or a mild putting-off (2 Kings 3:13; 2 Samuel 16:10). Since Jesus does act, he is not indifferent to the need; he is saying that what he does is set by his hour (the next sentence), not by a family request. The evidence for how sharp it is is balanced.

The address is courteous; Jesus uses it to the Samaritan woman (4:21), to Mary Magdalene (20:15) and to his mother from the cross (19:26). It is unusual for a son to use it to his mother, and the distance it sets matches the idiom (m1). The same address returns at the cross, when his hour has come.
"Woman" on its own can sound cold, but keeping it lets readers connect 2:4 with 19:26; the footnote says it was respectful. "Dear woman" would add warmth the word does not carry by itself.
For young readers "Woman" sounds rude, which the Greek is not. She is his mother, so Readable uses the address a son would use. The footnote gives the literal word.

decisions.choice: is that a matter for you and me? (B); why are you bringing this to me? (R)
alternatives: What is that to me and to you? (Literal)
decisions.reason: Both keep the idiom a question and keep its distance without making it rude; Readable says it plainly.

As in English: the Greek address is respectful, but "mujer" on its own can sound cold. Literal and Balanced keep it so readers can link 2:4 with 19:26; the footnote on meaning decision m2 says it was courteous. Readable says "Madre", the address a son would use.

decisions.choice: ¿Qué [nos importa eso] a mí y a ti? (L); ¿y eso qué tiene que ver con nosotros? (B); ¿por qué me lo dices a mí? (R)
decisions.reason: The idiom keeps a polite distance (meaning decision m1). "¿Qué tengo yo contigo?" suggests there is no bond between them, which is harsher than the Greek. Literal keeps the two persons; Balanced uses a natural Spanish question; Readable says it plainly.

As in English: the Greek address is respectful, but French "Femme" used to address someone sounds abrupt today. Literal and Balanced keep it so that readers can link 2:4 with 19:26, and the footnote on m2 says that it was respectful; "Madame" would make a son sound distant from his mother. Readable says "Mère", the address a son would use. Jesus says "tu" to her at every level, as French does within a family.

decisions.choice: Qu’[est-ce que cela fait], à moi et à toi (L); est-ce notre affaire, à toi et à moi ? (B); pourquoi viens-tu me dire cela ? (R)
alternatives: Qu’y a-t-il entre moi et toi ?
Quoi de commun entre moi et toi ?
decisions.reason: The idiom keeps a polite distance (m1). "Qu’y a-t-il entre moi et toi" and "Quoi de commun entre moi et toi" suggest that there is no bond between them, which is harsher than the Greek. Literal keeps the two datives ("à moi et à toi"); Balanced asks whether the matter is theirs to settle; Readable says it plainly.

γύναι is a respectful address in Greek. Calling a woman "Mwanamke!" to her face is rude in Swahili, so even Literal cannot keep the word without changing the tone. "Mama" is the respectful address to any older woman, so it is accurate at every level and also names her as his mother, as the English Readable does.

The Greek address is respectful, but "여자여" said to one's own mother sounds cold or even rude in Korean. Literal keeps the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable say "어머니", which keeps the respect and names her as his mother. The English keeps "Woman" at Balanced, so the Korean differs there.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to his mother in the polite style ("-나요", "-세요") and calls himself "저" (B, R)
alternatives: the plain style he uses to disciples and crowds ("-느냐")
decisions.reason: The plain style Jesus uses to others would be disrespectful from a son to his mother in Korean, and the Greek address is courteous. The polite style keeps the courtesy while the words still decline her request.

The Greek address is respectful. A bare "đàn bà" (woman) is rude in Vietnamese, so Literal uses the polite "Thưa bà", keeping the distance of the Greek word; Balanced and Readable name her as his mother, as the style guide asks, since a son calling his mother "bà" sounds cold.

decisions.choice: Jesus calls himself "con" to his mother in Balanced and Readable (also "Giờ của con" in the next sentence); Literal keeps the book-wide "Ta"
decisions.reason: Once she is addressed as "mẹ", Vietnamese requires the son to call himself "con"; "Ta" to one's mother sounds arrogant. Literal keeps "Ta" with "bà". A reviewer should decide whether "Ta" should give way to "con" at every level here and in 19:26.

source.text: οὔπω ἥκει ἡ ὥρα μου.

records.literal_gloss: Not yet has come the hour of me.

en.L: My hour has not yet come."
en.B: My hour has not yet come."
en.R: My time has not come yet."

es.L: Todavía no ha llegado mi hora».
es.B: Todavía no ha llegado mi hora».
es.R: Aún no es mi hora».

fr.L: Mon heure n’est pas encore venue. »
fr.B: Mon heure n’est pas encore venue. »
fr.R: Ce n’est pas encore {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} heure. »

sw.L: Saa {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} bado haijafika."
sw.B: Saa {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} bado haijafika."
sw.R: Wakati {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} bado haujafika."

ko.L: 내 때가 아직 오지 않았어요."
ko.B: 제 때가 아직 오지 않았어요."
ko.R: 아직 제 때가 오지 않았어요."

vi.L: Giờ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chưa đến."
vi.B: Giờ của con chưa đến."
vi.R: Chưa đến lúc của con."

decisions.choice: his hour: the time the Father has set, which John later shows to be his death and glorification
alternatives: only the right moment to act at this wedding
decisions.reason: This is the first mention of Jesus's hour. Later it "had not yet come" (7:30; 8:20) until "the hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified" (12:23; 13:1; 17:1). At Cana the sign shows his glory ahead of time (2:11). The hour is set by the Father, not by request.

alternatives: a question: has my hour not come?
decisions.reason: The manuscripts have no punctuation, and some early readers took it as a question. The SBLGNT punctuates it as a statement, and John's other uses of "not yet" with the hour are statements (7:30; 8:20).
Readable says "time" because "hour" sounds like sixty minutes; Literal and Balanced keep "hour" so the thread through the Gospel stays visible.

English Readable says "time" because "hour" sounds like sixty minutes. Spanish "mi hora" ("le llegó su hora") is everyday language for an appointed moment, so Readable keeps the word and the thread through the Gospel (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: heure at every level (Readable "Ce n’est pas encore mon heure")
decisions.reason: English Readable says "time" because "hour" sounds like sixty minutes. In French "son heure" ("son heure est venue", "ce n’est pas encore l’heure") is everyday language for an appointed moment, so Readable can keep the word and the thread through the Gospel (m1).

decisions.choice: the quotation opened in 2:4a closes at the end of this sentence
alternatives: close the quotation after 2:4a, as the English does
decisions.reason: Both sentences are Jesus's words to his mother, so French closes the quotation marks here, as other passages do when a speech runs across records.
"Saa" (hour) keeps the thread of Jesus's hour through the Gospel, as the book-wide choice for John asks. Readable says "wakati" (time), as the English Readable says "my time".

"때" is the appointed time and keeps the thread of Jesus's "hour" through the Gospel (7:30; 12:23; 13:1; 17:1). "시" is a clock hour and "시간" an amount of time, so neither carries the sense here. Korean needs no separate Readable word, unlike the English "my time".

source.text: λέγει ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ τοῖς διακόνοις· Ὅ τι ἂν λέγῃ ὑμῖν ποιήσατε.

records.literal_gloss: Says the mother of him to the servants, "Whatever he may say to you, do."

en.L: His mother says to the servants, "Whatever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to you, do [it]."
en.B: His mother said to the servants, "Do as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tells you, whatever it is."
en.R: His mother said to the servants, "Do anything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tells you."

es.L: Su madre dice a los sirvientes: «Lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:les|os}} diga, {{plural_you:háganlo|hacedlo}}».
es.B: Su madre dijo a los sirvientes: «{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:les|os}} diga».
es.R: Su madre les dijo a los sirvientes: «{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} cualquier cosa que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:les|os}} diga».

fr.L: Sa mère dit aux serviteurs : « Tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous dira, faites[-le]. »
fr.B: Sa mère dit aux serviteurs : « Quoi qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous dise, faites-le. »
fr.R: Sa mère a dit aux serviteurs : « Faites tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous dira. »

sw.L: Mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} anawaambia watumishi, "Lolote atakalowaambia, fanyeni."
sw.B: Mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} akawaambia watumishi, "Fanyeni lolote atakalowaambia."
sw.R: Mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} akawaambia watumishi, "Fanyeni chochote atakachowaambia."

ko.L: 그분의 어머니가 하인들에게 말한다. "그가 너희에게 무엇을 말하든지, [그대로] 하여라."
ko.B: 그분의 어머니가 하인들에게 말했다. "그가 너희에게 무엇을 시키든지 그대로 하여라."
ko.R: 예수의 어머니가 하인들에게 말했다. "그가 시키는 일은 무엇이든지 하여라."

vi.L: Mẹ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với những người phục vụ: "Điều gì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bảo các anh, hãy làm [theo]."
vi.B: Mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bảo những người phục vụ: "Ngài bảo gì, các anh cứ làm theo, dù là việc gì."
vi.R: Mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dặn những người phục vụ: "Ngài bảo gì thì các anh cứ làm theo nhé."

decisions.choice: an echo of Pharaoh's words about Joseph
decisions.reason: In the Greek Old Testament Pharaoh tells the hungry Egyptians, "Go to Joseph, and whatever he says to you, do" (Genesis 41:55). The wording is nearly the same. In both stories a need is met through the one others are told to obey.

decisions.choice: the household servants waiting on the feast
decisions.reason: The word means a servant or attendant; the church sense came later. The same people are called servants in verse 9.

decisions.choice: she trusts him to act, though he has just put her off
decisions.reason: Her words show she takes his reply as leaving room for him to act in his own way.
The household servants waiting on the feast (meaning decision m2). "Servidores" is also possible; "sirvientes" is the plain word.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms; él with the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: Every plural "you" in this passage is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). As in John 1, the deity_pronoun setting is on stressed pronouns for God or Christ (él, tú, mí).
These are the household servants waiting on the feast. "종" is kept for the Greek word for a slave (doulos) through the book, and "일꾼" suggests hired labourers.

decisions.choice: "Ngài" for Jesus in his mother's words to the servants
decisions.reason: She speaks of her son to the household servants. "Anh ấy" or "cậu ấy" would be natural for an ordinary son, but would set Jesus lower than the narrator does in the same verse; "Ngài" keeps the book-wide pronoun and the deity_pronoun setting.

source.text: ἦσαν δὲ ἐκεῖ λίθιναι ὑδρίαι ἓξ κατὰ τὸν καθαρισμὸν τῶν Ἰουδαίων κείμεναι, χωροῦσαι ἀνὰ μετρητὰς δύο ἢ τρεῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Were now there stone water jars six, according to the purification of the Jews standing, holding each measures two or three.

en.L: Now there were six stone water jars standing there according to the purification [rites] of the Jews, holding two or three measures each.
en.B: Six stone water jars stood there, kept for Jewish ritual washing; each held about {{units:20 to 30 gallons|two or three measures}}.
en.R: Six large stone jars for water were standing nearby. The Jewish people used jars like these for religious washing. Each jar held about {{units:20 to 30 gallons|two or three measures}}.

es.L: Y había allí seis tinajas de piedra, puestas para la purificación de los judíos, en cada una de las cuales cabían dos o tres medidas.
es.B: Allí había seis tinajas de piedra para los ritos judíos de purificación; en cada una cabían {{units:entre 80 y 120 litros|dos o tres medidas}}.
es.R: Cerca de allí había seis tinajas grandes de piedra para agua. El pueblo judío usaba tinajas como esas para lavarse según lo que mandaba su religión. En cada tinaja cabían {{units:entre 80 y 120 litros|dos o tres medidas}}.

fr.L: Or il y avait là six jarres de pierre, posées selon [l’usage de] la purification des Juifs, contenant chacune deux ou trois mesures.
fr.B: Six jarres de pierre se trouvaient là, destinées aux purifications rituelles juives ; chacune contenait environ {{units:80 à 120 litres|deux ou trois mesures}}.
fr.R: Il y avait là six grandes jarres de pierre pour l’eau. Le peuple juif utilisait ce genre de jarres pour les lavages que demandait sa religion. Chaque jarre contenait environ {{units:80 à 120 litres|deux ou trois mesures}}.

sw.L: Basi palikuwa na mitungi sita ya mawe ya maji imewekwa huko kwa ajili ya [desturi za] utakaso wa Wayahudi, kila mmoja ukichukua vipimo viwili au vitatu.
sw.B: Hapo palikuwa na mitungi sita ya mawe ya maji, iliyotumiwa kwa ajili ya kunawa kwa desturi ya Kiyahudi; kila mmoja ulichukua kama {{units:lita 80 hadi 120|vipimo viwili au vitatu}}.
sw.R: Karibu hapo palikuwa na mitungi sita mikubwa ya mawe ya kuwekea maji. Wayahudi walitumia mitungi ya namna hiyo kwa ajili ya kunawa kidini. Kila mtungi ulichukua kama {{units:lita 80 hadi 120|vipimo viwili au vitatu}}.

ko.L: 그런데 거기에는 유대인들의 정결 [예식]을 따라 돌로 된 물항아리 여섯 개가 놓여 있었는데, [하나에] 두세 메트레테스씩 들어가는 것이었다.
ko.B: 그곳에는 유대인의 정결 예식에 쓰는 돌 물항아리 여섯 개가 놓여 있었는데, 항아리 하나에 {{units:80에서 120리터|두세 메트레테스}}쯤 들어갔다.
ko.R: 그 근처에는 커다란 돌 항아리 여섯 개가 있었다. 유대인들은 이런 항아리에 물을 담아 두고, 종교적으로 깨끗하게 씻는 예식을 할 때 썼다. 항아리 하나에 물이 {{units:80에서 120리터|두세 메트레테스}}쯤 들어갔다.

vi.L: Ở đó có sáu chum đá đựng nước, đặt theo [lễ] thanh tẩy của người Do Thái, mỗi chum chứa hai hoặc ba thùng.
vi.B: Ở đó có sáu chum nước bằng đá, dùng cho việc tẩy uế theo nghi lễ của người Do Thái; mỗi chum chứa khoảng {{units:80 đến 120 lít|hai hoặc ba thùng}}.
vi.R: Gần đó có sáu cái chum lớn bằng đá để đựng nước. Người Do Thái dùng những chum như thế để tắm rửa theo nghi lễ tôn giáo. Mỗi chum chứa khoảng {{units:80 đến 120 lít|hai hoặc ba thùng}}.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the Jewish people and their customs
decisions.reason: John uses the word in several senses (see the note on the book's terms). Here it names the people whose purity customs these were; John explains them for readers who did not share them. Jesus, his mother and his disciples are Jews.

decisions.choice: stone jars kept for the washings that made people and vessels ritually clean
decisions.reason: Jewish custom washed hands and vessels before meals (Mark 7:3-4). Stone was used because, unlike clay, it was held not to become unclean (compare Leviticus 11:33, where an unclean clay pot must be broken). Stone vessels are common finds in first-century Judea and Galilee.

decisions.choice: two or three measures each: about 80 to 120 liters
decisions.reason: The measure named, μετρητής, was a liquid measure of about 39 liters. Each jar held two or three of them, so the six jars together held roughly 480 to 700 liters. The amount of wine in the sign is lavish.

decisions.choice: about {{units:20 to 30 gallons|two or three measures}}
alternatives: two or three measures at every level
twenty to thirty gallons in words
decisions.reason: The Greek measure (about 10 gallons, or 39 liters) means nothing to most readers, so Balanced and Readable give the modern equivalent by default, and the units setting shows the original "two or three measures". Numerals are used in measurements. Literal always keeps the ancient unit.
Where the word means the people, Balanced and Readable use "Jewish" (see the book's terms).

Spanish readers measure in liters, so the modern default is metric, as in French. The Greek measure held about 39 liters, so two or three of them make about 78 to 117 liters, rounded (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the original unit.
Here the word means the people whose customs these were (meaning decision m1), so no level speaks of leaders.

decisions.choice: environ {{units:80 à 120 litres|deux ou trois mesures}}
decisions.reason: French readers measure in litres, so the modern default is metric, not the US gallons of the English. The Greek measure held about 39 litres, so two or three of them make about 78 to 117 litres, rounded to "80 à 120 litres" (m3). The units setting shows the original "deux ou trois mesures"; Literal always keeps the ancient unit.

The measure held about 39 litres. Swahili-speaking countries use litres, so the metric figure is the default and the original measure the alternative; the English default is US gallons. Literal keeps the original measure.

Korean readers measure in litres, so the metric figure is the default and the Greek measure, transliterated as "메트레테스", is the alternative; the English default is US gallons. Literal keeps the original measure.

alternatives: the English US units (20 to 30 gallons)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese readers measure in liters, so the metric figure is the default and the original measure the alternative, as in French and Swahili; the English default is US gallons.
"Thùng" (a barrel or tub) is a plain Vietnamese word for a liquid measure; a transliteration would mean nothing to readers, and the footnote gives the size.

source.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Γεμίσατε τὰς ὑδρίας ὕδατος· καὶ ἐγέμισαν αὐτὰς ἕως ἄνω.

records.literal_gloss: Says to them the Jesus, "Fill the jars with water." And they filled them up to above.

en.L: Jesus says to them, "Fill the jars with water." And they filled them up to [the] top.
en.B: Jesus said to them, "Fill the jars with water." They filled them up to the top.
en.R: Jesus told the servants, "Fill the jars with water." So they filled the jars all the way to the top.

es.L: Jesús les dice: «{{plural_you:Llenen|Llenad}} de agua las tinajas». Y las llenaron hasta arriba.
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Llenen|Llenad}} de agua las tinajas». Y las llenaron hasta el borde.
es.R: Jesús les dijo a los sirvientes: «{{plural_you:Llenen|Llenad}} las tinajas con agua». Entonces ellos las llenaron hasta arriba.

fr.L: Jésus leur dit : « Remplissez les jarres d’eau. » Et ils les remplirent jusqu’en haut.
fr.B: Jésus leur dit : « Remplissez les jarres d’eau. » Ils les remplirent à ras bord.
fr.R: Jésus a dit aux serviteurs : « Remplissez les jarres avec de l’eau. » Alors ils les ont remplies jusqu’en haut.

sw.L: Yesu anawaambia, "Ijazeni mitungi maji." Nao wakaijaza mpaka juu.
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia, "Ijazeni mitungi maji." Wakaijaza mpaka juu.
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia watumishi, "Jazeni mitungi hii maji." Basi wakaijaza mitungi mpaka juu kabisa.

ko.L: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하신다. "항아리들에 물을 채워라." 그리고 그들이 그것들을 위까지 채웠다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "항아리에 물을 채워라." 그들은 항아리마다 물을 가장자리까지 가득 채웠다.
ko.R: 예수께서 하인들에게 말씀하셨다. "항아리에 물을 채워라." 그래서 하인들은 항아리마다 물을 넘칠 만큼 가득 채웠다.

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Hãy đổ nước đầy các chum." Và họ đổ đầy đến [tận] miệng.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu bảo họ: "Hãy đổ nước đầy các chum này." Họ đổ đầy đến tận miệng chum.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu bảo những người phục vụ: "Hãy đổ nước vào các chum cho đầy." Họ đổ nước đầy đến tận miệng chum.

decisions.reason: The servants filled the jars completely, so nothing else could have been added and the amount was as large as the jars allowed (2:6).
Readable names the people meant by "them" (verse 5).
As in English: Readable names the people meant (verse 5).

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to the servants in the plain style ("채워라")
decisions.reason: The style guide gives Jesus the plain style when he speaks to disciples, crowds and others; here he gives orders to household servants. This contrasts with the polite style he used to his mother in 2:4.

decisions.choice: historic present: Literal "nói" without "đã"; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past where Vietnamese needs it (whole passage)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese verbs do not change for tense, so leaving out "đã" keeps John's vivid present at Literal without strain; one decision for the passage.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἀντλήσατε νῦν καὶ φέρετε τῷ ἀρχιτρικλίνῳ· οἱ δὲ ἤνεγκαν.

records.literal_gloss: And he says to them, "Draw out now and carry to the master of the feast." And they carried.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Draw [some] out now and carry [it] to the master of the feast." And they carried [it].
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Now dip some out and carry it to the man in charge of the feast." And they did.
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Now take some out and bring it to the man in charge of the feast." So they did.

es.L: Y les dice: «{{plural_you:Saquen|Sacad}} ahora [un poco] y {{plural_you:llévenlo|llevadlo}} al encargado del banquete». Y [se lo] llevaron.
es.B: Luego les dijo: «Ahora {{plural_you:saquen|sacad}} un poco y {{plural_you:llévenselo|llevádselo}} al encargado del banquete». Y así lo hicieron.
es.R: Después les dijo: «Ahora {{plural_you:saquen|sacad}} un poco y {{plural_you:llévenselo|llevádselo}} al encargado de la fiesta». Y ellos lo hicieron.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Puisez maintenant, et portez[-en] au maître du repas. » Et ils [en] portèrent.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Maintenant, puisez-en et portez-en au maître du repas. » Et ils lui en portèrent.
fr.R: Ensuite, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a dit : « Maintenant, prenez-en un peu et apportez-en au responsable du repas. » Et c’est ce qu’ils ont fait.

sw.L: Naye anawaambia, "Sasa choteni, mkampelekee mkuu wa karamu." Nao wakapeleka.
sw.B: Kisha akawaambia, "Sasa choteni kidogo mkampelekee msimamizi wa karamu." Wakafanya hivyo.
sw.R: Kisha akawaambia, "Sasa toeni kidogo mkampelekee msimamizi wa karamu." Wakafanya hivyo.

ko.L: 그리고 그들에게 말씀하신다. "이제 떠서 잔치를 주관하는 이에게 가져가라." 그러자 그들이 가져갔다.
ko.B: 이어서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "이제 조금 떠서 잔치 책임자에게 가져다주어라." 그들은 그대로 했다.
ko.R: 그리고 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "이제 조금 떠서 잔치를 맡은 사람에게 갖다주어라." 그래서 하인들은 그렇게 했다.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Bây giờ hãy múc [ra] và đem đến cho người quản tiệc." Và họ đem đến.
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bảo họ: "Bây giờ hãy múc ra một ít và đem đến cho người phụ trách tiệc cưới." Họ làm theo.
vi.R: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Bây giờ hãy múc ra một ít, đem đến cho người lo việc tiệc." Họ liền làm theo.

alignments.target_span: man in charge of the feast

decisions.choice: the man presiding over the feast, in charge of the food and drink
alternatives: a guest chosen to preside over the drinking (compare Sirach 32:1-2)
decisions.reason: The word means the head of the dining room. Whether he was a senior servant or an honored guest is not clear, but either way he was responsible for the meal and could judge the wine.

decisions.choice: draw some out, most naturally from the jars just filled
alternatives: draw from the well, the jars being left full
decisions.reason: The verb is used of drawing water from a well (4:7, 15), and some read it so here. But nothing in the story mentions a well, and the order follows straight on from filling the jars. Every level says only "draw" or "take some out" without naming the source.

decisions.choice: the man in charge of the feast
decisions.reason: Plain words that fit either view of his role (m1).

decisions.choice: el encargado del banquete (L, B); el encargado de la fiesta (R)
decisions.reason: "Maestresala" is the traditional word but is now rare. "El encargado" names the man in charge without deciding whether he was a guest or a senior servant (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: le maître du repas (L, B); le responsable du repas (R)
decisions.reason: "Maître d’hôtel" now names a restaurant job, and "ordonnateur" is rare. "Le maître du repas" names the man presiding over the meal without deciding whether he was a guest or a steward (m1); "festin" sounds more literary than "repas". Readable uses the plainest word, "responsable".
"연회장" is the familiar church word, but today it is far more often heard as "banquet hall". A plain description of his role avoids the confusion.

source.text: ὡς δὲ ἐγεύσατο ὁ ἀρχιτρίκλινος τὸ ὕδωρ οἶνον γεγενημένον, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει πόθεν ἐστίν, οἱ δὲ διάκονοι ᾔδεισαν οἱ ἠντληκότες τὸ ὕδωρ, φωνεῖ τὸν νυμφίον ὁ ἀρχιτρίκλινος καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Πᾶς ἄνθρωπος πρῶτον τὸν καλὸν οἶνον τίθησιν, καὶ ὅταν μεθυσθῶσιν τὸν ἐλάσσω· σὺ τετήρηκας τὸν καλὸν οἶνον ἕως ἄρτι.

records.literal_gloss: When then tasted the master of the feast the water wine having become, and not he knew from where it is, but the servants knew, the ones having drawn the water, calls the bridegroom the master of the feast \v 10 and says to him, "Every man first the good wine sets, and when they have become drunk, the lesser; you have kept the good wine until now."

en.L: And when the master of the feast tasted the water that had become wine, and did not know where it was from (but the servants who had drawn the water knew), the master of the feast calls the bridegroom \v 10 and says to him, "{{gender:Everyone|Every man}} sets out the good wine first, and when [the guests] have become drunk, the lesser [wine]; you have kept the good wine until now."
en.B: The man in charge of the feast tasted the water that had become wine. He had no idea where it had come from, though the servants who had drawn the water knew. He called the bridegroom over \v 10 and said to him, "Every host sets out the good wine first, and the lesser wine once the guests are drunk. But you have kept back the good wine until now."
en.R: The man in charge of the feast tasted the water. It had turned into wine! He did not know where it had come from, but the servants who had taken out the water knew. So he called the bridegroom over. \v 10 He said, "A host always serves the good wine first. Then, when the guests have drunk so much that they cannot tell the difference, he serves the cheaper wine. But you have kept the good wine until now!"

es.L: Y cuando el encargado del banquete probó el agua convertida en vino —y no sabía de dónde era, pero los sirvientes que habían sacado el agua [lo] sabían—, el encargado del banquete llama al novio \v 10 y le dice: «{{gender:Todo el mundo|Todo hombre}} sirve primero el buen vino, y cuando [los invitados] se han embriagado, el de menor calidad; tú has guardado el buen vino hasta ahora».
es.B: El encargado del banquete probó el agua convertida en vino. No sabía de dónde había salido, aunque los sirvientes que habían sacado el agua sí lo sabían. Entonces llamó al novio \v 10 y le dijo: «Todo anfitrión sirve primero el buen vino, y el de menor calidad cuando los invitados ya están borrachos. ¡Pero tú has guardado el buen vino hasta ahora!».
es.R: El encargado de la fiesta probó el agua. ¡Se había convertido en vino! No sabía de dónde había salido, pero los sirvientes que habían sacado el agua sí lo sabían. Entonces llamó al novio. \v 10 Le dijo: «Siempre se sirve primero el vino bueno. Después, cuando los invitados han bebido tanto que ya no notan la diferencia, se sirve el vino más barato. ¡Pero tú has guardado el vino bueno hasta ahora!».

fr.L: Et quand le maître du repas eut goûté l’eau devenue vin — il ne savait pas d’où il venait, mais les serviteurs qui avaient puisé l’eau [le] savaient —, le maître du repas appelle le marié \v 10 et lui dit : « {{gender:Tout le monde|Tout homme}} sert d’abord le bon vin, et quand [les invités] sont ivres, le moins bon ; toi, tu as gardé le bon vin jusqu’à maintenant. »
fr.B: Le maître du repas goûta l’eau changée en vin. Il ne savait pas d’où venait ce vin, mais les serviteurs qui avaient puisé l’eau le savaient. Il appela le marié \v 10 et lui dit : « Celui qui reçoit sert toujours d’abord le bon vin, puis le moins bon quand les invités sont ivres. Mais toi, tu as gardé le bon vin jusqu’à maintenant ! »
fr.R: Le responsable du repas a goûté l’eau. Elle était devenue du vin ! Il ne savait pas d’où venait ce vin, mais les serviteurs qui avaient puisé l’eau, eux, le savaient. Alors il a appelé le marié. \v 10 Il lui a dit : « D’habitude, on sert le bon vin en premier. Puis, quand les invités ont tellement bu qu’ils ne sentent plus la différence, on sert le vin moins bon. Mais toi, tu as gardé le bon vin jusqu’à maintenant ! »

sw.L: Na mkuu wa karamu alipoyaonja maji yaliyokuwa yamegeuka divai, wala hakujua ilikotoka (lakini watumishi waliochota maji walijua), mkuu wa karamu anamwita bwana harusi \v 10 na kumwambia, "Kila mtu huandaa divai nzuri kwanza, na [wageni] wakishalewa, ndipo [huleta] iliyo duni; wewe umeiweka divai nzuri mpaka sasa."
sw.B: Msimamizi wa karamu aliyaonja maji yaliyokuwa yamegeuka divai. Hakujua ilikotoka, ingawa watumishi waliochota maji walijua. Akamwita bwana harusi \v 10 akamwambia, "Kila mwenye karamu huandaa divai nzuri kwanza, kisha divai duni wageni wakishalewa. Lakini wewe umeiweka divai nzuri mpaka sasa."
sw.R: Msimamizi wa karamu akayaonja maji. Yalikuwa yamegeuka divai! Hakujua ilikotoka, lakini watumishi waliochota maji walijua. Basi akamwita bwana harusi. \v 10 Akamwambia, "Mwenye karamu siku zote huwapa wageni divai nzuri kwanza. Kisha, wakishakunywa sana hata wasiweze kutofautisha, huwaletea divai ya bei nafuu. Lakini wewe umeiweka divai nzuri mpaka sasa!"

ko.L: 그런데 잔치를 주관하는 이가 포도주가 된 물을 맛보았을 때, 그는 그것이 어디서 온 것인지 알지 못했으나 (물을 떠 온 하인들은 알았다), 잔치를 주관하는 이가 신랑을 부르고 \v 10 그에게 말한다. "사람은 누구나 처음에 좋은 포도주를 내놓고, [손님들이] 취하면 덜 좋은 [것을 내놓습니다]. 그런데 당신은 좋은 포도주를 지금까지 남겨 두셨군요."
ko.B: 잔치 책임자는 포도주가 된 물을 맛보았다. 그는 그 포도주가 어디서 났는지 몰랐지만, 물을 떠 온 하인들은 알고 있었다. 잔치 책임자는 신랑을 불러 \v 10 말했다. "잔치를 여는 사람은 누구나 좋은 포도주를 먼저 내놓고, 손님들이 취한 뒤에야 덜 좋은 포도주를 내놓습니다. 그런데 당신은 좋은 포도주를 지금까지 아껴 두셨군요."
ko.R: 잔치를 맡은 사람이 그 물을 맛보았다. 물이 포도주로 바뀌어 있었다! 그는 이 포도주가 어디서 났는지 몰랐지만, 물을 떠 온 하인들은 알고 있었다. 그래서 그는 신랑을 불렀다. \v 10 그가 말했다. "잔치를 여는 사람은 보통 좋은 포도주를 먼저 내놓아요. 그리고 손님들이 많이 마셔서 맛을 잘 모르게 되면, 그보다 싼 포도주를 내놓지요. 그런데 당신은 좋은 포도주를 지금까지 남겨 두셨네요!"

vi.L: Và khi người quản tiệc nếm nước đã hóa thành rượu, và không biết [rượu ấy] từ đâu đến (nhưng những người phục vụ đã múc nước thì biết), người quản tiệc gọi chú rể \v 10 và nói với anh ấy: "Ai cũng dọn rượu ngon ra trước, và khi [khách] đã say thì [dọn rượu] kém hơn; còn anh đã giữ rượu ngon cho đến bây giờ."
vi.B: Người phụ trách tiệc cưới nếm nước đã hóa thành rượu. Ông không biết rượu ấy từ đâu ra, dù những người phục vụ đã múc nước thì biết. Ông gọi chú rể đến \v 10 và nói: "Chủ tiệc nào cũng đem rượu ngon ra trước, rồi khi khách đã say mới đem rượu kém hơn. Còn anh lại giữ rượu ngon cho đến bây giờ."
vi.R: Người lo việc tiệc nếm thử nước ấy. Nước đã hóa thành rượu! Ông không biết rượu từ đâu ra, nhưng những người phục vụ đã múc nước thì biết. Vậy ông gọi chú rể đến. \v 10 Ông nói: "Ai đãi tiệc cũng mời rượu ngon trước. Đến khi khách đã uống nhiều, không còn phân biệt được nữa, mới đem rượu loại thường ra. Còn anh lại để dành rượu ngon đến bây giờ!"

alignments.target_span: The man in charge of the feast

decisions.choice: the water had really become wine
alternatives: the water only seemed to be wine
decisions.reason: The perfect participle describes a finished change: what was water now was wine. John does not say when or how it happened, only that it had.

decisions.choice: he did not know where it came from
decisions.reason: "Where from" is a question John keeps returning to about Jesus himself (7:27-28; 9:29-30; 19:9). The servants know; the man in charge does not.

alternatives: have drunk freely, without being drunk
decisions.reason: The verb normally means to be drunk (Acts 2:15; 1 Thessalonians 5:7). The man in charge is stating a general rule about what hosts usually do, not saying that the guests at Cana were drunk.

decisions.choice: he speaks to the bridegroom because the groom's household provided the wine
decisions.reason: The bridegroom gets the credit for wine he did not provide.

decisions.choice: every host: anyone giving a feast
decisions.reason: "Every person" here is a general rule about whoever gives a feast; it is not limited to men.
The general word for a person refers to whoever gives the feast, so "host" says it plainly and needs no setting. Literal keeps the general word with the gender setting.
The Greek has the plain adjective "good", not a superlative. Keeping "good" also keeps the repeated word that ties the rule to the man's surprise.

decisions.choice: drunk so much that they cannot tell the difference
decisions.reason: Readable spells out why hosts do this, which the rule implies (m3).

decisions.choice: {{gender:Todo el mundo|Todo hombre}} (L); todo anfitrión (B); se sirve (R)
decisions.reason: The general word for a person means whoever gives the feast (meaning decision m5). Literal keeps it with the gender setting; Balanced says "anfitrión", which in Spanish, unlike French "hôte", means only the host; Readable uses the impersonal "se", the plain Spanish way to state a custom.

decisions.choice: han bebido tanto que ya no notan la diferencia
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable spells out why hosts do this (meaning decision m3).

The general word for a person means whoever gives the feast (m5), as English "Every host" says. French "hôte" means both host and guest, so Balanced says "celui qui reçoit"; Readable uses the generic "on", the plain French way to state a custom. Both are already inclusive, so they need no setting. Literal keeps the general word with the gender setting, "{{gender:Tout le monde|Tout homme}}".

decisions.choice: kila mtu (L); kila mwenye karamu (B); mwenye karamu (R); no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "every man" as the traditional alternative. "Kila mtu" already means anyone, man or woman, and "kila mwanamume" would mean only males, so Swahili has no span, as in John 1.
"사람" and "누구나" already include men and women in Korean, so the English gender span has nothing to change here. The same holds for "사람" in 2:24-25.

decisions.choice: The man in charge speaks to the bridegroom politely, with the honorific "-시-" ("두셨군요")
decisions.reason: He addresses the host of the feast, whose household provided the wine, so Korean needs a polite style; the exclamatory "-군요" ("-네요" at Readable) carries his surprise.

decisions.choice: "chú rể" for the bridegroom, addressed as "anh"
decisions.reason: "Chú rể" is the everyday modern word; "chàng rể" is literary. The older man in charge of the feast calls the young groom "anh".

source.text: ταύτην ἐποίησεν ἀρχὴν τῶν σημείων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἐφανέρωσεν τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: This did [as] beginning of the signs the Jesus in Cana of the Galilee and revealed the glory of him, and believed in him the disciples of him.

en.L: This, [the] beginning of the signs, Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} revealed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Jesus did this at Cana in Galilee as the first of the signs. In it {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} revealed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: This was the first sign Jesus did. It happened at Cana in Galilee. By it {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Este principio de las señales hizo Jesús en Caná de Galilea, y manifestó su gloria, y sus discípulos creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Así, en Caná de Galilea, Jesús hizo la primera de las señales. Con ella manifestó su gloria, y sus discípulos creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Esta fue la primera señal que hizo Jesús. Sucedió en Caná, en Galilea. Con ella mostró su gloria, y sus discípulos creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Ce commencement des signes, Jésus le fit à Cana de Galilée, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} manifesta {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples crurent en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Ce fut là, à Cana de Galilée, le premier des signes que fit Jésus. Par ce signe, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} manifesta {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples crurent en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: C’était le premier signe que Jésus faisait. Cela s’est passé à Cana, en Galilée. Par ce signe, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a montré {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples ont cru en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Hii, mwanzo wa ishara, Yesu aliifanya katika Kana ya Galilaya, na akaudhihirisha utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakamwamini.
sw.B: Yesu alifanya hivi huko Kana ya Galilaya kama ishara ya kwanza. Kwa hiyo aliudhihirisha utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakamwamini.
sw.R: Hii ilikuwa ishara ya kwanza aliyoifanya Yesu. Ilitokea Kana ya Galilaya. Kwa ishara hiyo alionyesha utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakamwamini.

ko.L: 예수께서 이것을 표적들의 처음으로 갈릴리의 가나에서 행하시어 자신의 영광을 드러내셨고, 그분의 제자들이 그분을 믿었다.
ko.B: 예수께서 갈릴리 가나에서 이 일을 첫 표적으로 행하셨다. 이 표적으로 그분께서는 자신의 영광을 드러내셨고, 제자들은 그분을 믿었다.
ko.R: 이것이 예수께서 행하신 첫 번째 표적이었다. 이 일은 갈릴리 가나에서 일어났다. 이 표적으로 예수께서는 자신의 영광을 보여 주셨고, 제자들은 예수를 믿었다.

vi.L: Việc này, khởi đầu các dấu lạ, Đức Giê-xu đã làm tại Ca-na thuộc Ga-li-lê, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã bày tỏ vinh quang của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đã làm việc này tại Ca-na, xứ Ga-li-lê, là dấu lạ đầu tiên của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Qua đó {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bày tỏ vinh quang của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và các môn đồ tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đây là dấu lạ đầu tiên Đức Giê-xu làm. Việc ấy xảy ra tại Ca-na, vùng Ga-li-lê. Qua dấu lạ này, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho thấy vinh quang của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: the first, the beginning of the signs
alternatives: merely the first in a numbered list
decisions.reason: The word is "beginning", not just "first": it opens the series of signs that runs through the Gospel. John counts the second at 4:54.

decisions.choice: sign: a deed that points beyond itself to who Jesus is
decisions.reason: John's word stresses meaning, not power. He gathers the purpose of the signs at the end: they are written so that readers may believe (20:30-31).
This takes up 1:14, "we have seen his glory". The glory is God's presence shown in Jesus, here in an abundant gift.

decisions.choice: believed in him: put their trust in him
decisions.reason: "Believe in" with a person, John's usual phrase, means trusting the person, not only accepting a fact. Their response is the one the signs aim at; contrast 2:23-24.
Balanced shows that the glory was revealed through this sign; the Greek joins the clauses with a plain "and".

The book-wide choice for John: never "milagro", because John's word points beyond the deed (meaning decision m2). "Señal" is the everyday Spanish word for something that points to something else; "signo" now sounds technical.
As in English: shows that the glory was revealed through this sign.
"표적" is a sign that points beyond itself, John's sense; "기적" means "miracle" and loses that. "표징" is the Catholic word.

"Phép lạ" means miracle and loses John's point that the deed points beyond itself. "Dấu chỉ" is closer to "sign" but is mostly Catholic usage; "dấu lạ" is familiar to Protestant readers and keeps the idea of a sign. A reviewer should weigh "dấu chỉ".

en.L: After this {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went down to Capernaum, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and the brothers and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, and there they stayed not many days.
en.B: After this {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went down to Capernaum, together with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples. They did not stay there many days.
en.R: After this, Jesus went down to the town of Capernaum with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples. They stayed there only a few days.

es.L: Después de esto bajó a Capernaúm, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y su madre y los hermanos y sus discípulos, y allí se quedaron no muchos días.
es.B: Después de esto bajó a Capernaúm con su madre, sus hermanos y sus discípulos. Allí se quedaron pocos días.

fr.L: Après cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} descendit à Capharnaüm, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère et les frères et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, et là ils ne restèrent pas de nombreux jours.
fr.B: Après cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} descendit à Capharnaüm avec {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} frères et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. Ils n’y restèrent que peu de jours.
fr.R: Après cela, Jésus est descendu dans la ville de Capharnaüm avec {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} frères et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. Ils sont restés là seulement quelques jours.

sw.L: Baada ya hayo alishuka Kapernaumu, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} na mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na ndugu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na huko walikaa siku si nyingi.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo alishuka Kapernaumu pamoja na mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Hawakukaa huko siku nyingi.
sw.R: Baada ya hayo, Yesu alishuka kwenda mji wa Kapernaumu pamoja na mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Walikaa huko siku chache tu.

ko.L: 이 일 후에 그분께서는 그분의 어머니와 형제들과 그분의 제자들과 함께 가버나움으로 내려가셨다. 그리고 거기서 여러 날을 머물지는 않았다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 예수께서는 어머니와 형제들과 제자들과 함께 가버나움으로 내려가셨다. 그들은 그곳에 여러 날 머물지는 않았다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 예수께서는 어머니와 형제들과 제자들과 함께 가버나움이라는 마을로 내려가셨다. 그들은 거기서 며칠만 지냈다.

vi.L: Sau việc này, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi xuống Ca-bê-na-um, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và các anh em và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; và họ ở lại đó không nhiều ngày.
vi.B: Sau đó, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xuống Ca-bê-na-um cùng với mẹ, các anh em và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ ở lại đó không lâu.
vi.R: Sau việc này, Đức Giê-xu xuống thị trấn Ca-bê-na-um với mẹ, các anh em và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ chỉ ở đó vài ngày.

decisions.choice: went down: from the hill country to the lakeshore
decisions.reason: Capernaum lay on the shore of the Sea of Galilee, well below Cana in the hills.

The word is the ordinary one for brothers, and his brothers appear again in 7:3-10. Christians differ on whether they were sons of Mary, sons of Joseph by an earlier marriage, or close relatives; the text does not settle it, so every level says "brothers". Specific men are meant here, so the gender setting does not apply.

decisions.choice: not many days: only a few days
decisions.reason: An understatement for a short stay; the next verse moves on to Passover in Jerusalem.
Readable names Jesus at the start of a new scene.
Specific men are meant, Jesus's brothers (compare 7:3-10), so the gender setting does not apply. The footnote on meaning decision m2 gives the views of who they were.

Specific men are meant, Jesus's brothers (m2; compare 7:3-10), so the inclusive setting does not apply, and "frères et sœurs" would add people the Greek does not name. The footnote on m2 gives the views of who they were.
"동생들" would decide that they were younger brothers, a question the footnote leaves open. Specific men are meant, so there is no gender span.

Vietnamese must otherwise say whether brothers are older ("anh") or younger ("em"). "Anh em" names brothers without deciding that question, which the footnote leaves open (younger brothers, half brothers, cousins).

source.text: Καὶ ἐγγὺς ἦν τὸ πάσχα τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ἀνέβη εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ὁ Ἰησοῦς.

records.literal_gloss: And near was the Passover of the Jews, and went up to Jerusalem the Jesus.

en.L: And the Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
en.B: The Jewish festival of Passover was approaching, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
en.R: The Jewish Passover festival was coming soon, so Jesus traveled up to Jerusalem.

es.L: Y estaba cerca la Pascua de los judíos, y Jesús subió a Jerusalén.
es.B: Se acercaba la fiesta judía de la Pascua, y Jesús subió a Jerusalén.
es.R: Pronto iba a ser la fiesta judía de la Pascua, así que Jesús subió a Jerusalén.

fr.L: Et la Pâque des Juifs était proche, et Jésus monta à Jérusalem.
fr.B: La fête juive de la Pâque approchait, et Jésus monta à Jérusalem.

sw.L: Na Pasaka ya Wayahudi ilikuwa karibu, na Yesu akapanda kwenda Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Sikukuu ya Kiyahudi ya Pasaka ilikuwa imekaribia, na Yesu akapanda kwenda Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the Jewish people, whose festival it was
decisions.reason: John explains Jewish festivals for readers who did not keep them (also 6:4; 11:55). The phrase does not set Jesus apart from his people: he goes up to keep the feast.

decisions.choice: Passover: the spring festival recalling the exodus from Egypt
decisions.reason: Passover remembered God's rescue of Israel from Egypt (Exodus 12), and Jewish men were to go up to the sanctuary for it (Deuteronomy 16:16). John names three Passovers (2:13; 6:4; 11:55); at the last Jesus dies.

decisions.choice: went up: Jerusalem is high in the hills
decisions.reason: One always "goes up" to Jerusalem (Psalm 122:4), as one goes down to Capernaum (2:12).
The word means the people here, so Balanced and Readable say "Jewish" (see the book's terms).
Readable shows that he went to keep the feast, which the context implies.

source.text: καὶ εὗρεν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τοὺς πωλοῦντας βόας καὶ πρόβατα καὶ περιστερὰς καὶ τοὺς κερματιστὰς καθημένους, καὶ ποιήσας φραγέλλιον ἐκ σχοινίων πάντας ἐξέβαλεν ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ τά τε πρόβατα καὶ τοὺς βόας, καὶ τῶν κολλυβιστῶν ἐξέχεεν τὰ κέρματα καὶ τὰς τραπέζας ἀνέστρεψεν, καὶ τοῖς τὰς περιστερὰς πωλοῦσιν εἶπεν· Ἄρατε ταῦτα ἐντεῦθεν, μὴ ποιεῖτε τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός μου οἶκον ἐμπορίου.

records.literal_gloss: And he found in the temple the ones selling oxen and sheep and doves and the money changers sitting, \v 15 and having made a whip out of cords, all he drove out from the temple, the both sheep and the oxen, and of the money changers he poured out the coins and the tables overturned, \v 16 and to the ones the doves selling he said, "Take these things from here; not make the house of the Father of me a house of trade."

en.L: And in the temple {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found those selling cattle and sheep and doves, and the money changers sitting [there], \v 15 and having made a whip out of cords, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drove all out of the temple, both the sheep and the cattle, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned the tables, \v 16 and to those selling the doves {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Take these things from here; do not make the house of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father a house of trade."
en.B: In the temple courts {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found people selling cattle, sheep and doves, and money changers sitting there. \v 15 He made a whip out of cords and drove them all out of the temple courts, sheep and cattle alike. He spilled the money changers' coins and turned their tables over. \v 16 To the dove sellers {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Take all this away from here! Do not make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father's house a house of business."
en.R: In the temple courtyard Jesus found people selling cattle, sheep and doves for sacrifices. Others were sitting there changing money. \v 15 So Jesus made a whip out of ropes. He chased all of them out of the temple area, both sheep and cattle. He threw the money changers' coins on the ground and knocked over their tables. \v 16 He told the people selling doves, "Take these things out of here! Stop using {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father's house as a place to buy and sell!"

es.L: Y encontró en el templo a los que vendían bueyes y ovejas y palomas, y a los cambistas sentados [allí], \v 15 y, haciendo un látigo de cuerdas, echó a todos fuera del templo, y las ovejas y los bueyes, y desparramó las monedas de los cambistas y volcó las mesas, \v 16 y a los que vendían las palomas les dijo: «{{plural_you:Quiten|Quitad}} esto de aquí; no {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} de la casa de mi Padre una casa de comercio».
es.B: En los atrios del templo encontró a gente que vendía reses, ovejas y palomas, y a los cambistas sentados allí. \v 15 Hizo un látigo de cuerdas y echó a todos de los atrios del templo, tanto a las ovejas como a las reses. Desparramó por el suelo las monedas de los cambistas y volcó sus mesas. \v 16 A los vendedores de palomas les dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Saquen|Sacad}} todo esto de aquí! No {{plural_you:conviertan|convirtáis}} la casa de mi Padre en una casa de negocios».
es.R: En el patio del templo, Jesús encontró a gente que vendía reses, ovejas y palomas para los sacrificios. Otros estaban sentados allí cambiando dinero. \v 15 Entonces Jesús hizo un látigo con cuerdas. Echó a todos del patio del templo, tanto a las ovejas como a las reses. Tiró al suelo las monedas de los que cambiaban dinero y les volcó las mesas. \v 16 A los que vendían palomas les dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Saquen|Sacad}} esto de aquí! ¡{{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} de usar la casa de mi Padre como un mercado!».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} trouva dans le temple ceux qui vendaient des bœufs et des moutons et des colombes, et les changeurs assis [là], \v 15 et, ayant fait un fouet avec des cordes, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les chassa tous du temple, et les moutons et les bœufs, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} répandit la monnaie des changeurs et renversa les tables, \v 16 et à ceux qui vendaient les colombes {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Enlevez cela d’ici ; ne faites pas de la maison de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père une maison de négoce. »
fr.B: Dans la cour du temple, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} trouva des marchands de bœufs, de moutons et de colombes, et des changeurs assis là. \v 15 Il fit un fouet avec des cordes et les chassa tous de la cour du temple, moutons et bœufs compris. Il répandit par terre la monnaie des changeurs et renversa leurs tables. \v 16 Aux marchands de colombes, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Enlevez tout cela d’ici ! Cessez de faire de la maison de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père une maison de commerce ! »
fr.R: Dans la cour du temple, Jésus a trouvé des gens qui vendaient des bœufs, des moutons et des colombes pour les sacrifices. D’autres étaient assis là pour changer l’argent. \v 15 Alors Jésus a fait un fouet avec des cordes. Il les a tous chassés de la cour du temple, les moutons comme les bœufs. Il a jeté par terre les pièces de ceux qui changeaient l’argent, et il a renversé leurs tables. \v 16 Il a dit aux vendeurs de colombes : « Enlevez tout cela d’ici ! Arrêtez de faire de la maison de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père un marché ! »

sw.L: Na katika hekalu aliwakuta wale waliokuwa wakiuza ng'ombe na kondoo na njiwa, na wabadilishaji fedha wakiwa wameketi [hapo], \v 15 naye akatengeneza mjeledi wa kamba, akawafukuza wote kutoka hekaluni, kondoo na ng'ombe pia, na akazimwaga sarafu za wabadilishaji fedha na kuzipindua meza, \v 16 na wale waliokuwa wakiuza njiwa akawaambia, "Ondoeni vitu hivi hapa; msiifanye nyumba ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kuwa nyumba ya biashara."
sw.B: Katika nyua za hekalu aliwakuta watu wakiuza ng'ombe, kondoo na njiwa, na wabadilishaji fedha wameketi hapo. \v 15 Akatengeneza mjeledi wa kamba, akawafukuza wote kutoka nyua za hekalu, kondoo na ng'ombe pia. Akazimwaga sarafu za wabadilishaji fedha na kuzipindua meza zao. \v 16 Akawaambia wauza njiwa, "Ondoeni vitu hivi hapa! Msiifanye nyumba ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kuwa nyumba ya biashara."
sw.R: Katika uwanja wa hekalu Yesu aliwakuta watu wakiuza ng'ombe, kondoo na njiwa kwa ajili ya dhabihu. Wengine walikuwa wameketi hapo wakibadilisha fedha. \v 15 Basi Yesu akatengeneza mjeledi kwa kamba. Akawafukuza wote kutoka eneo la hekalu, kondoo na ng'ombe pia. Akazimwaga chini sarafu za wabadilishaji fedha na kuzipindua meza zao. \v 16 Akawaambia wale waliokuwa wakiuza njiwa, "Toeni vitu hivi hapa! Acheni kuifanya nyumba ya Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kuwa mahali pa kununua na kuuza!"

ko.L: 그리고 성전에서 그분께서는 소와 양과 비둘기를 파는 사람들과, 앉아 있는 돈 바꾸는 사람들을 보셨다. \v 15 그리고 끈으로 채찍을 만드시어, 양과 소 할 것 없이 모두를 성전에서 내쫓으시고, 돈 바꾸는 사람들의 동전을 쏟으시고 상들을 엎으셨다. \v 16 그리고 비둘기를 파는 사람들에게 말씀하셨다. "이것들을 여기에서 치워라. 내 아버지의 집을 장사의 집으로 만들지 마라."
ko.B: 성전 뜰에서 그분께서는 소와 양과 비둘기를 파는 사람들과, 거기 앉아 있는 환전상들을 보셨다. \v 15 그분께서는 끈으로 채찍을 만드셔서 양과 소 할 것 없이 모두 성전 뜰에서 내쫓으셨다. 환전상들의 돈을 쏟아 버리시고 그들의 상을 뒤엎으셨다. \v 16 그리고 비둘기 파는 사람들에게 말씀하셨다. "이것들을 여기서 치워라! 내 아버지의 집을 장터로 만들지 마라."
ko.R: 예수께서는 성전 뜰에서 제물로 바칠 소와 양과 비둘기를 파는 사람들을 보셨다. 다른 사람들은 거기 앉아서 돈을 바꿔 주고 있었다. \v 15 그래서 예수께서는 밧줄로 채찍을 만드셨다. 그리고 모두 성전 뜰 밖으로 쫓아내셨는데, 양과 소도 다 쫓아내셨다. 돈 바꾸는 사람들의 동전을 바닥에 쏟아 버리시고 그들의 상을 뒤엎으셨다. \v 16 그리고 비둘기 파는 사람들에게 말씀하셨다. "이것들을 여기서 치워라! 내 아버지의 집을 물건을 사고파는 곳으로 쓰지 마라!"

vi.L: Và trong đền thờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy những người bán bò, chiên và bồ câu, và những người đổi tiền đang ngồi [đó], \v 15 và sau khi làm một cái roi bằng dây thừng, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đuổi tất cả ra khỏi đền thờ, cả chiên lẫn bò, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đổ tiền của những người đổi tiền và lật đổ các bàn, \v 16 và với những người bán bồ câu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Hãy đem những thứ này ra khỏi đây; đừng biến nhà của Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thành nhà buôn bán."
vi.B: Trong sân đền thờ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy người ta bán bò, chiên, bồ câu, và những người đổi tiền ngồi ở đó. \v 15 Ngài lấy dây thừng làm một cái roi, rồi đuổi tất cả họ ra khỏi sân đền thờ, cả chiên lẫn bò. Ngài hất đổ tiền của những người đổi tiền và lật nhào bàn của họ. \v 16 Ngài nói với những người bán bồ câu: "Hãy dọn hết những thứ này ra khỏi đây! Đừng biến nhà Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thành nơi kinh doanh."
vi.R: Trong sân đền thờ, Đức Giê-xu thấy người ta bán bò, chiên và bồ câu để dâng tế lễ. Có những người khác ngồi đổi tiền. \v 15 Vì vậy Đức Giê-xu lấy dây thừng làm một cái roi. Ngài đuổi tất cả bọn họ ra khỏi khu đền thờ, cả chiên lẫn bò. Ngài hất tiền của những người đổi tiền xuống đất và xô ngã bàn của họ. \v 16 Ngài bảo những người bán bồ câu: "Đem những thứ này ra khỏi đây! Đừng dùng nhà của Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm chỗ mua bán nữa!"

decisions.choice: the temple area as a whole, with its outer courts
decisions.reason: This word names the whole temple complex, including the large outer court where trade went on. In verses 19-21 Jesus uses a different word, for the sanctuary itself.

alternatives: private trade with no link to worship
decisions.reason: Pilgrims needed animals without defect for sacrifice; doves were the offering of the poor (Leviticus 5:7; 12:8). The temple tax had to be paid in an approved coin (Exodus 30:13), so money changers exchanged coins. The trade served worship, but it was being done inside the temple courts.

decisions.choice: he drove them all out, the sheep and cattle included; whether the sellers are meant as well is left open
alternatives: only the animals were driven out
the sellers and the animals were driven out
decisions.reason: "All" is masculine and is followed by "both the sheep and the cattle", which may explain it or add to it. The whip of cords suits driving animals; the text does not say he struck anyone. Every level keeps "all" without deciding.

decisions.choice: my Father's house: Jesus calls God his own Father
alternatives: the house of our father (Israel's God, in general)
decisions.reason: The first time in John that Jesus calls God "my Father" (compare Luke 2:49). The authorities' challenge in verse 18 responds to the authority he claims.
Zechariah's vision of the last day ends, "there will no longer be a trader in the house of the LORD". The link is in the idea, not the wording, so it is uncertain.

decisions.choice: temple courts / temple courtyard / temple area
decisions.reason: Distinguishes the temple area from the sanctuary (m1), which keeps the word "temple" clear for verses 19-21. Literal keeps "temple" for both words with the note.
"Oxen" now suggests animals that pull ploughs; these were cattle for sacrifice.
Readable says why animals were sold in the temple (m2).
Keeps the repeated word "house", which sets God's house against a trading house.

decisions.choice: los atrios del templo (B); el patio del templo (R); el templo (L)
decisions.reason: This word means the whole temple area with its courts, where the market stood (meaning decision m1). The word for the sanctuary itself comes in verses 19-21 and is "templo" at every level, so Balanced and Readable name the courts here to keep the two apart. "Atrios" is the traditional word for the temple courts; Readable uses the plain "patio".
"Bueyes" suggests animals that pull ploughs; these were cattle for sacrifice. "Ganado" would include the sheep.

decisions.choice: una casa de comercio (L); una casa de negocios (B); un mercado (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the repeated word "casa", which sets God's house against a trading house. Readable says plainly what it had become.
Spanish "a todos", like the Greek, does not say whether the sellers are meant as well as the animals (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: la cour du temple (B, R); le temple (L)
decisions.reason: This word means the whole temple area with its courts, where the market stood (m1); the word for the sanctuary itself comes in verses 19-21 and is "le temple" at every level. Balanced and Readable say "la cour du temple" so that the two stay distinct; "parvis" and "esplanade" are less familiar to most readers. Literal keeps "le temple" for both Greek words, with the note.

decisions.choice: une maison de négoce (L); une maison de commerce (B); un marché (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the repeated word "maison", which sets God's house against a trading house. "Trafic" now suggests illegal dealing, which the Greek word for trade does not say. Balanced "Cessez de" gives the force of the present command (stop making); Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: hekalu (L); nyua za hekalu (B); uwanja wa hekalu, eneo la hekalu (R)
decisions.reason: ἱερῷ is the whole temple area with its outer courts, where the market was. Literal says "hekalu"; Balanced and Readable say the courts or the grounds, so that "hekalu" alone can stand for the sanctuary, ναὸν, in verses 19-21, as the book-wide choice for John has it.
Literal keeps the Greek's repeated "house"; Balanced uses "장터" (marketplace), a natural Korean picture of what the temple courts had become; Readable says it plainly.
Korean can leave the object of "내쫓다" unstated, which keeps the Greek open on whether the sellers were driven out with the animals.
"Chiên" is the Bible word Vietnamese readers know from "Chiên Con của Đức Chúa Trời" (1:29) and the shepherd of chapter 10; keeping it ties these passages together.

en.R: His disciples remembered that the Scripture says, "My strong love for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house will consume {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
