sw.R: Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakakumbuka kwamba Maandiko yanasema, "Upendo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mkuu kwa nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} utaniteketeza."

ko.L: 그분의 제자들은 이렇게 기록되어 있다는 것을 기억했다. "주의 집을 위한 열심이 나를 삼킬 것이다."
ko.B: 그분의 제자들은 이렇게 기록된 말씀을 기억했다. "주의 집을 향한 열정이 나를 집어삼킬 것이다."
ko.R: 제자들은 성경에 이렇게 쓰여 있는 것을 떠올렸다. "주의 집을 사랑하는 뜨거운 마음이 나를 삼켜 버릴 것이다."

vi.L: Các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhớ lại rằng có lời chép: "Lòng nhiệt thành vì nhà Chúa sẽ ăn nuốt con."
vi.B: Các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhớ lại lời đã chép: "Lòng nhiệt thành vì nhà Chúa sẽ thiêu đốt con."
vi.R: Các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhớ lại lời Kinh Thánh: "Lòng con yêu mến nhà Chúa nồng nàn, sẽ thiêu đốt con như lửa."

decisions.reason: The words come from Psalm 69, the prayer of a righteous man who suffers for his loyalty to God. John quotes the same psalm at 15:25 and alludes to it at the cross (19:28-29).
In Psalm 69:10 the verb is past. John's form is future, pointing ahead: Jesus's devotion to God's house will cost him his life.

decisions.choice: zeal: burning devotion to God's honor
decisions.reason: The word is used of passionate loyalty to God (compare Numbers 25:11, where Phinehas is zealous for God's honor), not of envy.

decisions.choice: they remembered it then, as they watched
alternatives: they remembered it only after the resurrection, like verse 22
decisions.reason: Verse 22 explicitly says "when he was raised"; this verse does not, so it most likely describes their thought at the time. Either is possible.
The verb is literally "eat up". Literal and Balanced keep the image of eating; Readable uses the plainest word for being used up.
"Zeal" is an uncommon word for young readers; Readable says what it means and makes "my" explicit, since the zeal is the speaker's.

"Wivu" can mean zeal for God, but to most readers today it means jealousy or envy. "Ari" is burning eagerness, which is the sense in the meaning note. Literal keeps the picture of eating (itanila, will eat me up); Balanced says it will consume me (itaniteketeza).

decisions.choice: Mi amor ardiente por (R); el celo (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Celo" is the usual biblical word, but in everyday Spanish it more often means jealousy. Readable says what it means (meaning decision m3), as the English does.
As in English: Literal and Balanced keep the image of eating; Readable uses the plainest word for being used up.
Korean does not address God with "당신" in a psalm; "주" is the established second-person word for God in Korean prayer and psalms, and keeps the quotation addressed to God.

decisions.choice: "nhà Chúa" and "con": the psalmist addresses God as "Chúa" and calls himself "con"; no deity_pronoun spans
alternatives: "nhà Ngài ... Ta" with spans as the English does
decisions.reason: In Vietnamese prayer one speaks to God with the noun "Chúa" and of oneself as "con". These are words of address, not pronouns, so they take no setting; the words are the Psalm's before they are Jesus's.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθησαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Τί σημεῖον δεικνύεις ἡμῖν, ὅτι ταῦτα ποιεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: Answered therefore the Jews and said to him, "What sign show you to us, that these things you do?"

en.L: So the Jews answered and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "What sign do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show us, since {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do these things?"
en.B: The Jewish leaders then said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "What sign do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} show us to justify doing these things?"
en.R: Then the Jewish leaders in the temple asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "What sign can {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give us to show that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have the right to do this?"

es.L: Respondieron, pues, los judíos y le dijeron: «¿Qué señal nos muestras, ya que haces estas cosas?».
es.B: Entonces los dirigentes judíos le dijeron: «¿Qué señal nos muestras para justificar lo que haces?».
es.R: Entonces los dirigentes judíos que estaban en el templo le preguntaron: «¿Qué señal puedes darnos para demostrar que tienes derecho a hacer esto?».

fr.L: Les Juifs répondirent donc et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Quel signe nous montres-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, puisque {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fais ces choses ? »
fr.B: Les autorités juives {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent alors : « Quel signe nous montres-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pour justifier ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fais ? »
fr.R: Alors les chefs juifs qui étaient au temple {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé : « Quel signe peux-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous donner pour montrer que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as le droit de faire cela ? »

sw.L: Basi Wayahudi wakajibu, wakamwambia, "Unatuonyesha ishara gani, kwa kuwa unafanya mambo haya?"
sw.B: Basi viongozi wa Wayahudi wakamwambia, "Unatuonyesha ishara gani kuthibitisha kwamba una mamlaka ya kufanya mambo haya?"
sw.R: Kisha viongozi wa Wayahudi waliokuwa hekaluni wakamwuliza, "Utatupa ishara gani kuonyesha kwamba una mamlaka ya kufanya hivi?"

ko.L: 그러자 유대인들이 대답하여 그분께 말했다. "당신이 이런 일들을 하니, 무슨 표적을 우리에게 보이겠습니까?"
ko.B: 그러자 유대 지도자들이 예수께 말했다. "당신이 이런 일을 해도 된다는 것을 보여 줄 무슨 표적이 있습니까?"
ko.R: 그러자 성전에 있던 유대 지도자들이 예수께 물었다. "당신에게 이런 일을 할 권리가 있다는 것을 무슨 표적으로 보여 주겠습니까?"

vi.L: Vậy người Do Thái đáp lại và nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ông cho chúng tôi thấy dấu lạ gì, vì ông làm những việc này?"
vi.B: Các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái liền hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ông lấy dấu lạ nào cho chúng tôi thấy để chứng tỏ ông có quyền làm những việc này?"
vi.R: Bấy giờ các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái trong đền thờ hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ông có thể làm dấu lạ gì để chứng tỏ ông có quyền làm việc này?"

decisions.choice: the Jews: the temple authorities in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: They demand to know by what right he acts in the temple, which is the authorities' question (compare 1:19, where priests and Levites are sent from Jerusalem, and Mark 11:27-28). It is not the Jewish people as a whole: Jesus, his disciples and the worshipers are Jews.

decisions.choice: responded to what he had done
decisions.reason: No one has asked anything; "answered" here means they reacted to his actions.

decisions.choice: a sign that would show his right to do these things
alternatives: what sign do you show, because you do these things?
decisions.reason: The clause gives the reason a sign is needed: since he acts with such authority, he must prove it. John's signs are given, not produced on demand (compare 6:30).
Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: los dirigentes judíos (B, R); los judíos (L)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the temple authorities in Jerusalem (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable name them, as in 1:19. Jesus and his disciples are Jews too; "los judíos" alone could suggest the whole people stood against him. The word John wrote is "los judíos".

decisions.choice: les autorités juives (B); les chefs juifs (R); les Juifs (L)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the temple authorities in Jerusalem (m1), so Balanced and Readable name them, as the English does. Jesus and his disciples are Jews too; "les Juifs" alone could suggest the whole people stood against him. The footnote on m1 gives the word John wrote, which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: The leaders speak to Jesus in the formal style but with "당신" and no honorific "-시-"
decisions.reason: They are challenging him, so the respectful "-십니까" that people use to Jesus elsewhere does not fit; open contempt ("-느냐") would overstate a demand that is not yet hostile. "당신" with "-습니까" is formal and cool.

decisions.choice: the temple authorities call Jesus "ông" and themselves "chúng tôi"; no deity_pronoun spans in their words
decisions.reason: "Ông" is the polite but distant address of officials who challenge him; "Thầy" would grant him a respect they withhold. "Ông" is a noun of address, so it takes no setting.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Answered Jesus and said to them, "Destroy the temple this, and in three days I will raise it."

en.L: Jesus answered and said to them, "Tear down this temple, and in three days I will raise it up."
en.B: Jesus replied, "Tear this temple down, and I will raise it up again within three days."
en.R: Jesus answered, "If you tear down this temple, I will raise it up again in three days."

es.L: Respondió Jesús y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Derriben|Derribad}} este templo, y en tres días lo levantaré».
es.B: Jesús les respondió: «{{plural_you:Derriben|Derribad}} este templo, y en tres días lo volveré a levantar».
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Si {{plural_you:ustedes derriban|vosotros derribáis}} este templo, yo lo volveré a levantar en tres días».

fr.L: Jésus répondit et leur dit : « Démolissez ce temple, et en trois jours je le relèverai. »
fr.B: Jésus leur répondit : « Démolissez ce temple, et je le relèverai en trois jours. »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Si vous démolissez ce temple, je le relèverai en trois jours. »

sw.L: Yesu akajibu, akawaambia, "Bomoeni hekalu hili, nami katika siku tatu nitalisimamisha."
sw.B: Yesu akawajibu, "Bomoeni hekalu hili, nami nitalisimamisha tena katika siku tatu."
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Mkilibomoa hekalu hili, nitalisimamisha tena katika siku tatu."

ko.L: 예수께서 대답하여 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "이 성전을 허물어라. 그리고 사흘 안에 내가 그것을 일으키겠다."
ko.B: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "이 성전을 허물어라. 그러면 내가 사흘 만에 다시 일으켜 세우겠다."
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "너희가 이 성전을 허물면, 내가 사흘 만에 다시 일으켜 세우겠다."

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đáp và nói với họ: "Hãy phá đền thờ này đi, và trong ba ngày {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ dựng nó lên."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Các người cứ phá đền thờ này đi, trong ba ngày {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ dựng lại."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Nếu các người phá đền thờ này, thì trong ba ngày {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ dựng nó lên lại."

decisions.choice: the sanctuary: the house of God itself
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the word for the sanctuary building where God's presence dwelt, not the word used in verses 14-15 for the whole temple area. Verse 21 uses the same word of his body.

decisions.choice: a command with the force of a condition: if you destroy it
decisions.reason: The command is a challenge, not a wish: if they destroy it, he will raise it. Either way the destroyers are the hearers. Mark 14:58 and 15:29 show that his words were later twisted against him.

decisions.choice: raise: used both of putting up a building and of raising the dead
decisions.reason: The verb has both senses, and verse 22 uses it of the resurrection. Every level keeps "raise" so the double meaning stays.
The verb means to undo or pull down; for a building "tear down" is the natural word. It departs from the familiar "destroy", which also fits.
Readable states the condition the command implies (m2), so it does not sound like an invitation.

decisions.choice: derribar ... levantar; templo at every level
decisions.reason: "Derribar" is the natural verb for pulling down a building, and departs from the familiar "destruir", which also fits. "Levantar" is used both of putting up a building and of raising the dead, so the double meaning stays (meaning decision m3). This is the word for the sanctuary itself (m1), so every level says "templo".
As in English: Readable states the condition the command implies (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Démolissez ce temple ... je le relèverai; "temple" at every level
decisions.reason: This is the word for the sanctuary itself (m1), so every level says "temple", which keeps the link with "le temple de son corps" in verse 21. "Démolir" is the natural verb for pulling down a building, as English "tear down". "Relever" is used both of putting a building back up and of raising someone, so it keeps the double sense of the Greek verb (m3); "rebâtir" would lose the second.

decisions.choice: nitalisimamisha (I will make it stand up)
decisions.reason: ἐγερῶ is said both of putting up a building and of raising the dead. Swahili has no one verb for both: "kujenga" (build) loses the resurrection, and "kufufua" (raise the dead) cannot be said of a building. "Kusimamisha" (make stand up) is used of erecting a building and can be heard of raising someone up, so the double sense survives in part. For review by a native speaker.
"일으키다" is used both of putting a building up and of raising the dead, so Korean keeps the Greek double sense that 2:21-22 explains. "짓다" would lose it.
No Vietnamese verb covers both raising a building and raising the dead. "Dựng lên" is what the hearers understood and what verse 20 answers; verses 21-22 and the footnote give the other sense.
The style guide's form for Jesus speaking to opponents and officials; it is firm without being rude.

source.text: εἶπαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Τεσσεράκοντα καὶ ἓξ ἔτεσιν οἰκοδομήθη ὁ ναὸς οὗτος, καὶ σὺ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερεῖς αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Said therefore the Jews, "Forty and six years was built the temple this, and you in three days will raise it?"

en.L: So the Jews said, "[In] forty-six years this temple was built, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will raise it up in three days?"
en.B: The Jewish leaders said, "Forty-six years this temple has been under construction, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will raise it up in three days?"
en.R: The Jewish leaders said, "People have been building this temple for forty-six years! Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} really raise it up in three days?"

es.L: Dijeron, pues, los judíos: «[En] cuarenta y seis años fue edificado este templo, ¿y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} en tres días lo levantarás?».
es.B: Los dirigentes judíos le respondieron: «Hace cuarenta y seis años que se está construyendo este templo, ¿y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} lo vas a levantar en tres días?».
es.R: Los dirigentes judíos dijeron: «¡Llevan cuarenta y seis años construyendo este templo! ¿De verdad {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} lo vas a levantar en tres días?».

fr.L: Les Juifs dirent donc : « [En] quarante-six ans ce temple a été bâti, et {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, en trois jours, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} le relèveras ? »
fr.B: Les autorités juives répliquèrent : « Cela fait quarante-six ans qu’on travaille à bâtir ce temple, et {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, en trois jours, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} le relèverais ? »
fr.R: Les chefs juifs ont dit : « On construit ce temple depuis quarante-six ans ! Et {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vas vraiment le relever en trois jours ? »

sw.L: Basi Wayahudi wakasema, "Hekalu hili lilijengwa [kwa] miaka arobaini na sita, na {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utalisimamisha katika siku tatu?"
sw.B: Viongozi wa Wayahudi wakasema, "Hekalu hili limekuwa likijengwa kwa miaka arobaini na sita, na {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utalisimamisha katika siku tatu?"
sw.R: Viongozi wa Wayahudi wakasema, "Watu wamekuwa wakilijenga hekalu hili kwa miaka arobaini na sita! Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utaweza kulisimamisha katika siku tatu?"

ko.L: 그러자 유대인들이 말했다. "이 성전은 사십육 년 동안 지어졌는데, 당신이 사흘 만에 그것을 일으키겠다는 겁니까?"
ko.B: 그러자 유대 지도자들이 말했다. "이 성전은 사십육 년째 짓고 있는데, 당신이 그것을 사흘 만에 일으켜 세우겠다는 말입니까?"
ko.R: 그러자 유대 지도자들이 말했다. "사람들이 이 성전을 사십육 년 동안이나 짓고 있습니다! 그런데 당신이 정말 사흘 만에 그것을 다시 일으켜 세우겠다는 말입니까?"

vi.L: Vậy người Do Thái nói: "Đền thờ này đã được xây [trong] bốn mươi sáu năm, mà ông sẽ dựng nó lên trong ba ngày sao?"
vi.B: Các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái nói: "Đền thờ này đã xây suốt bốn mươi sáu năm nay, mà ông sẽ dựng lại trong ba ngày sao?"
vi.R: Các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái nói: "Người ta đã xây đền thờ này bốn mươi sáu năm rồi! Ông thật sự sẽ dựng lại nó trong ba ngày sao?"

decisions.choice: the Jews: the same temple authorities as in verse 18
decisions.reason: They continue the exchange that began in verse 18.

decisions.choice: the temple has been under construction for forty-six years
alternatives: the sanctuary was completed forty-six years ago
it took forty-six years to build
decisions.reason: Herod the Great began rebuilding the temple about 20/19 BC (Josephus, Antiquities 15.380), and work went on for decades after this, so forty-six years from the start puts this Passover around AD 27/28. Since the work was still going on, the sense is most likely "has been under construction". But the sanctuary building itself was finished early, and the verb can also mean "was built" some time ago. The evidence is balanced.
The pronoun is stressed: forty-six years of work, and this man claims to do it in three days.
As in verse 18.
Readable shows the scorn of the emphatic pronoun (m3).
As in verse 18: the same temple authorities (meaning decision m1). The word John wrote is "los judíos".
The emphatic, scornful "tú" (meaning decision m3) is a stressed pronoun for Christ, so it takes the setting. Readable adds "De verdad" to show the scorn.

decisions.choice: les autorités juives (B); les chefs juifs (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 18: the same temple authorities (m1).
The emphatic "you" is scornful (m3). French shows incredulity with the conditional ("tu le relèverais ?"); Literal keeps the Greek future.

source.text: ἐκεῖνος δὲ ἔλεγεν περὶ τοῦ ναοῦ τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: That one however was speaking about the temple of the body of him.

en.L: But that one was speaking about the temple of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body.
en.B: But the temple {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant was {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own body.
en.R: But when Jesus said "temple", {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was talking about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own body.

es.L: Pero aquel hablaba del templo de su cuerpo.
es.B: Pero el templo del que hablaba era su propio cuerpo.
es.R: Pero cuando Jesús decía «templo», hablaba de su propio cuerpo.

fr.L: Mais celui-là parlait du temple de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps.
fr.B: Mais le temple dont {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parlait, c’était {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps.
fr.R: Mais quand Jésus disait « temple », {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parlait de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre corps.

sw.L: Lakini yule alikuwa akisema habari za hekalu la mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Lakini hekalu alilomaanisha lilikuwa mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu aliposema "hekalu", alikuwa akizungumza habari za mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}.

ko.L: 그러나 그분께서는 자신의 몸의 성전에 대하여 말씀하고 계셨다.
ko.B: 그러나 예수께서 말씀하신 성전은 자신의 몸이었다.
ko.R: 그러나 예수께서 "성전"이라고 하신 것은 자신의 몸을 두고 하신 말씀이었다.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thì nói về đền thờ của thân thể {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Nhưng đền thờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn nói đến chính là thân thể của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Nhưng khi Đức Giê-xu nói "đền thờ", {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn nói đến chính thân thể của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: the temple that is his body
alternatives: a temple belonging to his body
decisions.reason: The second noun says what the temple is: his body is the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: Jesus's body is the place where God dwells among people
decisions.reason: John has already said that the Word "pitched his tent" among us (1:14), as God's glory dwelt in the tabernacle. Now the sanctuary Jesus speaks of is himself; its destruction and raising are his death and resurrection (verse 22).

decisions.choice: that one, emphatic: he, unlike his hearers, meant something else
decisions.reason: John often lets hearers misunderstand Jesus and then explains (3:4; 4:11; 11:11-13).
Readable names the word being explained so young readers can follow the double meaning.
As in English: Readable names the word being explained so young readers can follow the double meaning.

source.text: ὅτε οὖν ἠγέρθη ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἐμνήσθησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι τοῦτο ἔλεγεν, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν τῇ γραφῇ καὶ τῷ λόγῳ ὃν εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς.

records.literal_gloss: When therefore he was raised from dead [ones], remembered the disciples of him that this he was saying, and they believed the Scripture and the word which said the Jesus.

en.L: So when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was raised out of [the] dead, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples remembered that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying this, and they believed the Scripture and the word which Jesus spoke.
en.B: Later, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been raised from the dead, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples remembered that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said this, and they believed the Scripture and what Jesus had said.
en.R: Later, after Jesus was raised from the dead, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples remembered that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said this. Then they believed the Scripture and what Jesus had said.

es.L: Por tanto, cuando fue levantado de entre los muertos, sus discípulos se acordaron de que decía esto, y creyeron a la Escritura y a la palabra que Jesús había dicho.
es.B: Más tarde, cuando fue resucitado de entre los muertos, sus discípulos recordaron que había dicho esto, y creyeron a la Escritura y a las palabras de Jesús.
es.R: Más tarde, cuando Jesús fue resucitado de entre los muertos, sus discípulos se acordaron de que había dicho esto. Entonces creyeron lo que decía la Escritura y lo que Jesús había dicho.

fr.L: Quand donc {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut relevé d’entre les morts, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples se souvinrent qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} disait cela, et ils crurent à l’Écriture et à la parole que Jésus avait dite.
fr.B: Plus tard, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut ressuscité d’entre les morts, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples se souvinrent qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait dit cela, et ils crurent à l’Écriture et à la parole que Jésus avait prononcée.
fr.R: Plus tard, quand Jésus a été ressuscité d’entre les morts, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples se sont souvenus qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait dit cela. Alors ils ont cru ce que disait l’Écriture et ce que Jésus avait dit.

sw.L: Basi alipofufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakakumbuka kwamba alikuwa akisema hivi, nao wakaliamini Andiko na neno ambalo Yesu alilisema.
sw.B: Baadaye, alipokuwa amefufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakakumbuka kwamba alikuwa amesema hivi, nao wakaliamini Andiko na maneno aliyokuwa amesema Yesu.
sw.R: Baadaye, Yesu alipofufuliwa kutoka kwa wafu, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakakumbuka kwamba alikuwa amesema hivi. Ndipo wakaliamini Andiko na maneno aliyokuwa amesema Yesu.

ko.L: 그러므로 그분께서 죽은 사람들 가운데서 일으켜지셨을 때, 그분의 제자들은 그분께서 이것을 말씀하셨던 것을 기억했고, 성경과 예수께서 하신 말씀을 믿었다.
ko.B: 나중에 예수께서 죽은 사람들 가운데서 일으킴을 받으신 뒤에, 제자들은 그분께서 이 말씀을 하셨던 것을 기억했다. 그리고 성경과 예수께서 하신 말씀을 믿었다.
ko.R: 나중에 하나님께서 예수를 죽은 사람들 가운데서 다시 살리신 뒤에, 제자들은 예수께서 이 말씀을 하셨던 것을 떠올렸다. 그제야 그들은 성경과 예수께서 하신 말씀을 믿었다.

vi.L: Vậy khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được sống lại từ [giữa] những người chết, các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhớ lại rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói điều này, và họ tin Kinh Thánh và lời Đức Giê-xu đã nói.
vi.B: Về sau, khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã được sống lại từ cõi chết, các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhớ lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói điều này, và họ tin Kinh Thánh cùng lời Đức Giê-xu đã nói.
vi.R: Về sau, khi Đức Giê-xu đã được sống lại từ cõi chết, các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhớ lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nói điều này. Bấy giờ họ tin Kinh Thánh và tin lời Đức Giê-xu đã nói.

decisions.choice: he was raised: God raised him
decisions.reason: The passive points to God as the one who raised him (compare Acts 2:24). In John, Jesus also says he will raise the temple himself (2:19; 10:17-18); the Gospel holds both together, so every level keeps the passive.

decisions.choice: the Scripture: a particular passage, most likely Psalm 69:10 quoted in verse 17
alternatives: a passage about rising, such as Psalm 16:10
decisions.reason: John uses the singular for a particular passage (as in 7:38; 19:24). The nearest one is the psalm in verse 17, but John may mean Scripture's witness to the resurrection in general (20:9). The evidence is balanced.

decisions.choice: the disciples understood only after the resurrection
decisions.reason: John says the same in 12:16, and Jesus promises that the Spirit will remind them of all he said (14:26).

decisions.choice: believed the Scripture and his word: trusted that they were true
alternatives: believed in them as in a person
decisions.reason: Here the verb takes a plain object, not "in": they now trusted what Scripture and Jesus had said.
Makes clear that John looks ahead to after the resurrection.

Literal uses "levantado", the verb of verses 19-20, so the reader sees the same word; Balanced and Readable use the usual Spanish word for the resurrection. All keep the passive, as meaning decision m1 asks; "resucitó" would lose it.

decisions.choice: creyeron a la Escritura (L, B); creyeron lo que decía (R)
decisions.reason: Here the verb takes a plain object (meaning decision m4): they believed that the Scripture and Jesus's words were true. Spanish marks this with "creer a" or "creer" + object, and keeps "creer en" for trusting a person, as in verses 11 and 23.
As in English: makes clear that John looks ahead to after the resurrection.

The verb is the one Jesus used in verse 19 and the leaders in verse 20. Literal says "relevé" so the reader sees the same word; Balanced and Readable use the usual French word for the resurrection. Both are passive, as the Greek is: God raised him (m1).

decisions.choice: crurent à l’Écriture (L, B); ont cru ce que disait l’Écriture (R)
decisions.reason: Here the verb takes a plain object, not "in": they believed that the Scripture and Jesus's word were true (m4). French marks this with "croire à" or "croire" + object, keeping "croire en" for believing in a person, as in verses 11 and 23.

The meaning note takes this as one passage, most likely the psalm quoted in verse 17, so Swahili uses the singular "Andiko" rather than "Maandiko" (the Scriptures). Jesus's saying is "neno" at Literal, lowercase, and "maneno" (words) at Balanced and Readable, so it is not confused with "Neno", the Word of 1:1.
The Greek passive means that God raised him. Korean passives of "일으키다" are stiff for new readers, so Readable names God as the one who acted rather than turn Jesus into the subject.

source.text: Ὡς δὲ ἦν ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν τῷ πάσχα ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, θεωροῦντες αὐτοῦ τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει·

records.literal_gloss: When then he was in the Jerusalem at the Passover at the feast, many believed in the name of him, seeing of him the signs which he was doing.

en.L: Now while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in Jerusalem at the Passover, at the feast, many believed in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, seeing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} signs which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was doing.
en.B: During the Passover festival, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in Jerusalem, many came to believe in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name as they watched the signs {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was doing.
en.R: While Jesus was in Jerusalem for the Passover festival, many people saw the signs {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was doing, and they believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y mientras estaba en Jerusalén, en la Pascua, durante la fiesta, muchos creyeron en su nombre, viendo las señales que hacía.
es.B: Durante la fiesta de la Pascua, mientras estaba en Jerusalén, muchos llegaron a creer en su nombre al ver las señales que hacía.
es.R: Mientras Jesús estaba en Jerusalén para la fiesta de la Pascua, mucha gente vio las señales que hacía, y creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Or, pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était à Jérusalem, à la Pâque, pendant la fête, beaucoup crurent en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom, voyant les signes qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} faisait.
fr.B: Pendant la fête de la Pâque, alors qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était à Jérusalem, beaucoup se mirent à croire en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom en voyant les signes qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} accomplissait.
fr.R: Pendant que Jésus était à Jérusalem pour la fête de la Pâque, beaucoup de gens ont vu les signes qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} faisait, et ils ont cru en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Basi alipokuwa Yerusalemu wakati wa Pasaka, katika sikukuu, wengi waliamini katika jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, wakiziona ishara {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} alizokuwa akizifanya.
sw.B: Wakati wa sikukuu ya Pasaka, alipokuwa Yerusalemu, watu wengi walianza kuliamini jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} walipoona ishara alizokuwa akifanya.
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa Yerusalemu kwa ajili ya sikukuu ya Pasaka, watu wengi waliona ishara alizokuwa akifanya, wakamwamini.

ko.L: 그런데 그분께서 유월절에, 명절에 예루살렘에 계실 때, 많은 사람이 그분께서 행하시는 그분의 표적들을 보면서 그분의 이름을 믿었다.
ko.B: 유월절 명절 동안 예수께서 예루살렘에 계실 때, 많은 사람이 그분께서 행하시는 표적들을 보고 그분의 이름을 믿게 되었다.
ko.R: 예수께서 유월절 명절을 지키러 예루살렘에 계시는 동안, 많은 사람이 예수께서 행하시는 표적들을 보았다. 그리고 그들은 예수를 믿었다.

vi.L: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở tại Giê-ru-sa-lem vào lễ Vượt Qua, trong kỳ lễ, nhiều người tin vào danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì thấy các dấu lạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm.
vi.B: Trong kỳ lễ Vượt Qua, khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở Giê-ru-sa-lem, nhiều người đã tin vào danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khi thấy các dấu lạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm.
vi.R: Khi Đức Giê-xu ở Giê-ru-sa-lem dự lễ Vượt Qua, nhiều người thấy các dấu lạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm, và họ tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: believed in his name: believed in him
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person, as in 1:12.

decisions.choice: their belief rested on the signs they watched
alternatives: they believed and also happened to see signs
decisions.reason: The participle gives the setting and the ground of their belief. John treats belief that rests only on signs as real but not yet deep (4:48; 20:29), and the next sentence shows its limit.
John has told only one sign so far, at Cana. These are others done in Jerusalem, which he mentions without telling (compare 20:30).
Readable gives the meaning of the idiom (m1).
As in English: Readable gives the meaning of the idiom (meaning decision m1).

source.text: αὐτὸς δὲ Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἐπίστευεν αὑτὸν αὐτοῖς διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν γινώσκειν πάντας καὶ ὅτι οὐ χρείαν εἶχεν ἵνα τις μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, αὐτὸς γὰρ ἐγίνωσκεν τί ἦν ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ.

records.literal_gloss: He himself however Jesus was not believing himself to them, because of the him knowing all [people], \v 25 and because not need he had that anyone should testify about the human being; he himself for knew what was in the human being.

en.L: But Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} was not entrusting {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to them, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knew {{gender:all people|all men}}, \v 25 and because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had no need that anyone should testify about {{gender:a human being|man}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} knew what was in {{gender:a human being|man}}.
en.B: But Jesus, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} part, would not trust {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to them, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knew {{gender:all people|all men}}. \v 25 He did not need anyone to testify to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about {{gender:people|man}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} knew what was in {{gender:a person|man}}.
en.R: But Jesus would not trust them, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knew {{gender:all people|all men}}. \v 25 No one needed to tell {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} what {{gender:people|men}} are like. He already knew what was in their hearts.

es.L: Pero Jesús mismo no se confiaba a ellos, porque conocía a {{gender:todos los seres humanos|todos los hombres}}, \v 25 y porque no tenía necesidad de que nadie diera testimonio acerca del {{gender:ser humano|hombre}}, pues {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo sabía lo que había en el {{gender:ser humano|hombre}}.
es.B: Pero Jesús, por su parte, no se fiaba de ellos, porque conocía a {{gender:todas las personas|todos los hombres}}. \v 25 No necesitaba que nadie le diera testimonio acerca de {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo sabía lo que hay en {{gender:cada persona|el hombre}}.
es.R: Pero Jesús no confiaba en ellos, porque conocía a {{gender:todas las personas|todos los hombres}}. \v 25 Nadie tenía que explicarle cómo son {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}. Él ya sabía lo que hay en el corazón de cada uno.

fr.L: Mais Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} ne se confiait pas à eux, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} connaissait {{gender:tout le monde|tous les hommes}}, \v 25 et parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’avait pas besoin que quelqu’un rende témoignage au sujet de {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}} ; car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} savait {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} ce qu’il y avait dans {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}.
fr.B: Mais Jésus, de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} côté, ne se fiait pas à eux, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} connaissait {{gender:tout le monde|tous les hommes}}. \v 25 Il n’avait pas besoin que quelqu’un {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rende témoignage sur {{gender:les êtres humains|l’homme}}, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} savait {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} ce qu’il y a dans {{gender:l’être humain|l’homme}}.
fr.R: Mais Jésus ne leur faisait pas confiance, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} connaissait {{gender:tout le monde|tous les hommes}}. \v 25 Personne n’avait besoin de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} expliquer comment sont {{gender:les gens|les hommes}}. Il savait déjà ce qu’il y avait dans leur cœur.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} hakuwaaminia nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kwa sababu aliwajua watu wote, \v 25 na kwa sababu hakuhitaji mtu yeyote amshuhudie habari za mwanadamu, kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alijua yaliyomo ndani ya mwanadamu.
sw.B: Lakini Yesu, kwa upande {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, hakuwaaminia nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kwa sababu aliwajua watu wote. \v 25 Hakuhitaji mtu yeyote amweleze habari za watu, kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alijua yaliyomo ndani ya mtu.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu hakuwaamini, kwa sababu aliwajua watu wote. \v 25 Hakuna aliyehitaji kumweleza watu walivyo. Yeye alijua tayari yaliyomo mioyoni mwao.

ko.L: 그러나 예수 그분은 자신을 그들에게 믿고 맡기지 않으셨는데, 그분께서 모든 사람을 아셨기 때문이며, \v 25 또 누가 사람에 대하여 증언할 필요가 그분께는 없었기 때문이다. 그분 자신이 사람 속에 무엇이 있는지 알고 계셨던 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 예수께서는 그들을 믿고 자신을 맡기지는 않으셨다. 모든 사람을 알고 계셨기 때문이다. \v 25 그분께는 사람에 대해 누가 증언해 줄 필요가 없었다. 사람 속에 무엇이 있는지 그분께서 친히 알고 계셨기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그러나 예수께서는 그들을 믿고 자신을 맡기지 않으셨다. 모든 사람을 잘 알고 계셨기 때문이다. \v 25 사람이 어떤지 누가 예수께 말해 줄 필요가 없었다. 예수께서는 사람들의 마음속에 무엇이 있는지 이미 알고 계셨다.

vi.L: Nhưng chính Đức Giê-xu không phó thác mình cho họ, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết hết mọi người, \v 25 và vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không cần ai làm chứng về con người, vì chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết điều gì ở trong con người.
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu không giao phó mình cho họ, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết rõ mọi người. \v 25 Ngài không cần ai làm chứng cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} về con người, vì chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết rõ trong lòng con người có gì.
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu không tin họ, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết rõ mọi người. \v 25 Không ai cần nói cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết con người ra sao. Ngài đã biết rõ trong lòng họ nghĩ gì.

decisions.choice: entrust himself: commit himself to them, rely on them
decisions.reason: This is the same verb as "believed" in verse 23. With an object and a person it means to entrust something to someone (Luke 16:11). John plays on the two senses: many believed in him, but he did not entrust himself to them. Since one word cannot carry both senses here, a footnote points out the wordplay.
The masculine plural is general here, as verse 25 shows by speaking of people in general.

decisions.choice: a human being, people in general
decisions.reason: The word is used in the general sense, so the gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: he knew what was in people
decisions.reason: Knowing the heart belongs to God (1 Samuel 16:7; Jeremiah 17:10). John has just shown it with Nathanael (1:47-48) and will show it again with the Samaritan woman (4:18, 29). The next chapter begins with "a man", using the same word, Nicodemus, as an example.

decisions.choice: entrust himself (L); trust himself to them (B); trust them (R)
decisions.reason: The verb cannot be "believe" here and still make sense. "Trust" keeps as much of the echo of verse 23 as possible; Readable says the plain meaning.
Inclusive default; Traditional one tap away.
Readable names the inner life, which "what was in" a person means.

decisions.choice: no se confiaba a ellos (L); no se fiaba de ellos (B); no confiaba en ellos (R)
decisions.reason: Verse 23 says many "creyeron en su nombre"; here John uses the same verb for Jesus, who did not entrust himself to them (meaning decision m1). Spanish has no single verb for both, and "no creía en ellos" would mean he had no hope in them. "Confiarse a" keeps "entrust himself"; Readable says the plain meaning.

decisions.choice: {{gender:todas las personas|todos los hombres}}; {{gender:el ser humano|el hombre}}
decisions.reason: The Greek means people in general (meaning decisions m2, m3), so the inclusive default says it plainly, with the traditional wording as the alternative.

decisions.choice: en el corazón de cada uno
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names the inner life. "Su corazón" would be unclear after "Él".

decisions.choice: ne se confiait pas à eux (L); ne se fiait pas à eux (B); ne leur faisait pas confiance (R)
decisions.reason: Verse 23 says many "crurent en son nom"; here John uses the same verb for Jesus, who did not entrust himself to them (m1). French has no single verb for both, and "ne croyait pas en eux" would mean that he had no hope in them, which is not the sense. "Se confier à" is the closest to "entrust oneself"; "se fier à" (Balanced) is the everyday word for relying on someone and comes from the same root as "foi" and "fidèle", keeping a faint echo; Readable says the plain meaning.
The Greek means people in general (m2, m3). French "l’homme" is read as generic less and less, so the inclusive default says it plainly, with the traditional wording as the alternative.

John plays on ἐπίστευεν: many believed in him (verse 23), but he did not entrust himself to them. "Kuaminia" (entrust to) is built on "kuamini" (believe), so Swahili keeps the play; Readable's "hakuwaamini" (did not trust them) keeps it too.

decisions.choice: watu wote; mwanadamu, mtu; no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "men" as the traditional alternative. "Watu", "mtu" and "mwanadamu" already include men and women, so Swahili has no span.

The Greek uses the verb "believe" in the sense "entrust", right after "many believed" in 2:23. "믿고 맡기다" means entrust and keeps the word "믿다", so Korean readers can still hear John's play on the two verses.
Vietnamese cannot use "tin" (believe) for entrusting oneself, so the play with "many believed" in verse 23 is lost; the meaning decision and its footnote point it out.

decisions.choice: "mọi người", "con người" with no gender spans
alternatives: gender spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Vietnamese words for people are already inclusive, so there is only one way to say this and no setting is needed (style guide section 7).
